Name: Ramona Strugariu
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Moldova deserves trust, it deserves the European perspective and the status of a candidate country, not because it is an important political moment to capitalize on, but because it has proven to us, in this crisis and beyond, that it deserves this trust...We cannot now, in the midst of a war of imperialism against democracy, ignore this vision. The Europe of the future is not just a space populated by rules; it is each country and each person won over to society and governments that fight for these rules and our values, em-brace them, and defend them. Moldova is doing just that. A country the size of a German state with a pro-European vein as big as the heart of Europe must be part of our construction. Economies grow and develop in a matter of years, but for nations to aspire to a European identity, it has taken decades. Today, the Republic of Moldova has this aspiration. Money, the rules adopted and respected, the accession chapters are the tools we must give. The goal is to bring it home, here, into the European family, even if it's not easy, even if it won't happen tomorrow.

Name: Heidi Hautala
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: And we must be very firm in our support for the European way of Moldova. I very much be-lieve that they are doing everything they can in this fragile situation to be able to finally get candidate status for membership. We have to help Moldova to get rid of this near-total dependency on Russian energy. We have to help them to balance the ownership of media, help them to get rid of disinfor-mation, which is really damaging their European way.

Name: Susanna Ceccardi
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: Even as a non-EU member, Moldova is still part of European culture. It shares our values and is linked to us through the Association Agreement. It is an increasingly important partner for Italy, with a trade exchange that reached 520 million euros in 2021, given Moldova's GDP of 12 billion.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: What the European Union and the European Parliament must do, of course, is to pay as much and as fast attention as possible to how Moldova can be supported both in humanitar-ian terms and with the necessary resources, and to give it a path towards the European Un-ion. Colleagues who say that the country has made efforts are right. Colleagues who say that not only the current situation should be the reason, but also the level of preparedness of the state at this very moment, are also right.

Name: Andrius Kubilius
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Let’s imagine a different picture now – one in which Moldova is a member of the EU. It’s very clear that it would be beneficial not only for Moldova, it would be beneficial for EU sta-bility in its neighbourhood...So let’s make a strategic conclusion from the lessons of this geopolitical crisis. Moldova membership in the European Union is needed not only for Moldova; it’s very much needed also for the European Union itself. And it’s very much needed for the perspective of a differ-ent Russia.

Name: Victor Negrescu
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: We are here for you. 600 million euros for the economic recovery plan, tens of millions of euros for humanitarian assistance, border security, refugee issues, and most importantly, for protecting the population in the context of rising energy prices...We are talking about investments to eliminate Moldova's dependence on the Russian Fed-eration. We are talking about strengthening democratic institutions. Not for us, but for you, the citizens of the Republic of Moldova. You deserve all our support and respect. Therefore, I once again call on my colleagues to support the rapid accession of the Republic of Moldova to the European Union.

Name: Dacian Cioloș
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Both the state and the citizens of the Republic of Moldova have rapidly and efficiently assisted Ukrainian refugees, acting as true European citizens. Despite facing their own diffi-culties due to Russia's aggression, Moldovans have welcomed and hosted refugees from Ukraine just as any citizens of an EU member state would...Through their behavior and actions, Moldova has already earned its place in the European Union, and our decision can only have one answer: "yes."...In the current circumstances, member states and the Union must show inventiveness and flexibility, and European leaders have no other option than to rise to the occasion and bring the Republic of Moldova into the European Union.

Name: Adam Bielan
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Why am I talking about Ukraine during a debate about Moldova? Because Moldova could be the next target of this madman, Putin. And I hope that in the case of Moldova, the European Union will be wise before the damage is done...We need to grant Moldova the status of a candidate country for the European Union. Finally, we need military aid, which Charles Michel has thankfully announced during his visit to the capital of Moldova this week. I hope that this time we will all be wise before the damage is done.

Name: Traian Băsescu
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the place of the Republic of Moldova is in the European Union. The impeccable response given by Chișinău in the context of the crisis in Ukraine, including the reception of refugees, is clear evidence that we share the same values and principles. The Republic of Moldova has demonstrated through its attitude and actions that it is a more European state than some EU member states or candidates. ...Where have the repeated concessions made to Moscow in the last 30 years led us? To an aggressive Russia, which has invaded Ukraine unprovoked and triggered a war and a human-itarian disaster that threatens peace and stability in Europe and the world. Therefore, I demand that the European Union grant the Republic of Moldova the status of candidate country for accession to the European Union

Name: Thijs Reuten
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: I’m both highly proud of and deeply concerned for Moldova. Proud because of the incredible assistance the Moldovan people have offered to the Ukrainians and because of Moldova’s unambiguous pro-European turn. But I am also concerned because Putin and his cronies have now set their sights on Moldova. ...Our Moldovan friends have clearly chosen democracy over dictatorship and we should be firmly with them on every step of their path to the EU membership they seek. We cannot afford complacency. I commend the Council and Commission’s pledge to boost defensive aid to Moldova, and this must be fast and ambitious.

Name: Vlad-Marius Botoş
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: today we are talking about Moldova and the progress it is making towards respecting demo-cratic and European values. We must acknowledge, esteemed colleagues, that the reforms of the past year and espe-cially the way they reacted when the war in Ukraine started, clearly show that Moldova is on the right path.

Name: Seán Kelly
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: over the years, Moldova has suffered with political instability and cases of corruption. How-ever, the leadership of Maia Sandu, who supports European values, now promises to reori-entate the country towards Europe in the fight against corruption. Moldova is showing great determination in the current crisis. Compared to its population of only 2.6 million people, no country has received more Ukrain-ian refugees than the Republic of Moldova, clearly showing that it is an ally ready to fight for a democracy and a European future...The EU must support Moldova in resisting such forceful attempts to bind it to Moscow so that the Moldovan people may choose their own path towards the future.

Name: Evin Incir
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Despite the many challenges in the country, they show their call of solidarity through receiv-ing the largest number of Ukrainian refugees per capita. We tend to very often in this Parliament talk about European fundamental values. This is actually European fundamental values in practice, in contrast to our own Member State, Hungary, which asks ‘How high?’ when Putin says ‘Jump’. I therefore welcome the decision by the Government of the Republic of Moldova to apply for EU membership.

Name: Eugen Tomac
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: over 50% of Moldovan citizens are citizens of the European Union, and we must give them a clear European perspective. Moldovan citizens have demonstrated through voting, through democratic means, that their place is here, with us, and we must provide this perspective.

Name: Tudor Ciuhodaru
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Good morning, Moldova, welcome to the European Union. Today, May 5, 2022, is a historic moment because the Parliament is voting and showing its solidarity with this European country, and I ask all of you to vote for this endeavor because it brings Moldova alongside Romania into the great European family.

Name: Maria Grapini
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: from the very beginning, as a Romanian and a member of the delegation for Moldova, I sup-port the resolution. I support everything that has been discussed here and what the Com-missioner said about aid...The citizens of the Republic of Moldova are Europeans. I know Moldova well from beyond the Prut River, which historically was separated from Moldova on the other side of the Prut. Therefore, assistance to Moldova from all perspectives, a European path, and immediate support.

Name: Joachim Stanisław Brudziński
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Moldova is an important candidate country for European Union membership. With a population of 3.5 million, it is a direct neighbor of Ukraine, making it a target for Russian influence. This is a significant factor in the process. Therefore, it is crucial for the EU to make every effort to ensure that lasting, real, and measurable ties with the West prevail over pro-Russian tendencies in the country...This beautiful country and its proud citizens should be assured that integration with the EU is a real alternative, a perspective for development, and above all, security. Having learned from the difficult experience of Russia's brutal aggression against Ukraine, let us build con-sistent and forward-looking alliances with countries that seek cooperation and integration, never forgetting Robert Schuman's idea of a united Europe in its diversity

Name: David McAllister
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The EU must be ready to provide more humanitarian, security and socio-economic assis-tance to the Republic of Moldova, the longer the Russian war against Ukraine lasts. This in-cludes: increasing the financial and technical assistance, including through a new proposal for macro-financial assistance; putting forward additional proposals aimed at ensuring the full liberalisation of transport and trade with the EU; working towards granting EU candidate status to the Republic of Moldova, in line with Article 49 of the Treaty of the European Union and on the basis of merit; in the meantime, working towards the full implementation of the Association Agreement with Moldova and its integration into the EU single market. The Moldovan authorities under President Maia Sandu are on the right track by adopting key reforms that will ensure Moldova´s compliance with the ‘Copenhagen criteria’. Let us pro-vide our full support to Moldova’s European aspirations.

Name: Marian-Jean Marinescu
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Today's Moldova, with Maia Sandu, reminds me of the generation of Walesa, Havel, Kohl. Europeans without doubts. After war, communism, and poverty, the EU was an unparalleled choice. It is the same today, especially for a country like Moldova, where the troops of the 14th Soviet Army, now Russian, turn the idea of war into a daily threat, and this has been going on for 30 years. Maia Sandu's Moldova looks at the EU and sees its future here, feel-ing at home and safe, offering people the sweet taste of victory and the warmth of the Euro-pean family. We must not fail to open the door for them. They are ours, our future is together, and that is why we must tell them as soon as possible: welcome to the EU, Moldovans!

Name: Dan-Ştefan Motreanu
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I support the candidate country status for the European Union for the Republic of Moldova. The concrete perspective of EU accession will boost the morale of the citizens of the Repub-lic of Moldova who feel threatened and are facing material difficulties. The longer the Rus-sian aggression against Ukraine continues, the more Moldova will need help from the Un-ion: humanitarian aid, security assistance, and economic support. It is essential that this aid be provided in the form of grants to stabilize the socioeconomic situation and strengthen the country's overall resilience.

Name: Dragoş Tudorache
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Through the hardship of multiple crises, and through the kindness of their solidarity with Ukrainian refugees, the Moldovans have spoken to us today about their aspirations, about their ambitions, about their European projections. That hardship, that solidarity and that commitment to European values is the most significant test of identity, of belonging, that a nation must pass in its path to integration...I am proud that our report is as clear as it can be: we want that the Republic of Moldova is given candidate status. Of course, the road to actual membership will be long and full of hard work, and the Moldovans understand that. Today, we’ve heard the President being highly realistic about this perspective. But the force of the political message itself is not to be underestimated...There are reforms to be done. Our report mentions a good number of key transformations that the country must go through: justice and anti—corruption, the banking sector, energy security and diversification, and economic convergence, administrative reform. // The key political takeaway, the key political conclusion for me from today’s debate is that Moldova’s commitment to Europe is no longer just words. It is felt in the drive to reform the judiciary and to strengthen the rule of law. It is felt in how they hosted half a million refugees in their country, and how they withstand Russian pressure. It is a commitment that comes with risks and costs, and though they’re not doing it with guns in their hands, Moldovan citizens are fighting alongside their Ukrainian neighbours for the European dream, and for the values that bring us together. All that is needed now is our voice saying, without hesitation, that the Republic of Moldova’s rightful place is by our side.

Name: Olivér Várhelyi
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: We take very good note of your call to grant candidate status to Moldova in line with Article 49 of the Treaty on European Union and on the basis of merit. We understand the importance of the EU membership application for the Moldovan people. Following the request by the Council, the Commission has swiftly launched its work on the opinion. In this regard, I would like to commend the swift replies of the Moldovan authorities to both parts of our questionnaire. This is crucial in preparing our assessment. ..I want to reassure you that the Commission remains fully committed to Moldova and will continue to provide help and assistance for its pressing needs while continuing our long—term reforms mentioned in your report, including in the justice, energy and public administration sectors.

Name: Andrzej Halicki
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: This is something that we also need to cooperate with Moldovan society, and I think that the anticipated bright future is achievable. We can do it together, and candidate country status has to be granted as soon as possible, at the same time as it should be for Ukraine. It’s very important. It’s a political decision. But as Dragoş Tudorache said, there are many challenges. We are facing many tough, complicated reforms. I’m very glad to see this strong leadership because many things are done...Moldova is important for our common security. It is also our benefit to have Moldova as a secure well—developed country within our family, and we have to do it as fast as we can. So, for the President, the confirmation from the House: yes, you are a part of Europe. Long live Moldova! Long live Europe with Moldova together!

Name: Juozas Olekas
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The report also welcomes Moldova’s EU application. We support the country’s efforts to become a full member of the European family. Of course, there is still a big round of reforms facing Moldova, including justice reform and the approximation of its law with the European ones. But I believe that candidate status would galvanise reform efforts and would give a clear vision for its citizens.

Name: Ramona Strugariu
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The context of this report has been continuously evolving, both positively with the submission of Moldova's accession request, and negatively with the invasion of Ukraine. Due to this context, our message today is crucial: we stand with the Republic of Moldova more than ever. We want them to join the Union, and above all, we stand with them in implementing the bold reforms that the authorities in Chișinău have initiated...Establishing a support group for the Republic of Moldova, following the model already created for Ukraine, would allow us to better accompany reforms in the judiciary, the fight against corruption, economic recovery, and future accession negotiations. Finally, a word about justice reform and anti-corruption efforts. I want to encourage the authorities in Chișinău to continue with the same determination on this path. These sectors are fundamental to provide the citizens of the Republic of Moldova with the future they deserve and deserve together with us here in the European Union...They are waiting, and we are all waiting for Moldova to join the European family.

Name: Viola Von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Moldova is truly European. It has a European government that, in a short time, managed to make significant democratic improvements. It has generous people who have received thousands of Ukrainian fleeing the war...Moldova needs to continue pro—democratic reforms, combat corruption and uphold fundamental freedoms, and make sure that democratic development creates a foundation for economic progress so that Moldovans use their talents and skills to generate prosperity in their country. I strongly believe in the European future of Moldova, and for that to happen, we need to secure its European presence now.

Name: Bernhard Zimniok
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: The planned EU enlargement is not only entirely wrong but also highly dangerous. It is wrong because both the Balkan countries and the Republic of Moldova hardly meet any of the Copenhagen criteria, which are prerequisites for EU accession. It is also wrong because the highly corrupt Moldova - currently ranked 105th in the Corruption Perceptions Index - would be a net recipient for many years. Who will pay for that? ...So, not only would we be bringing a highly corrupt state into the EU, which would be a net recipient for decades, but we could also be dragged into direct conflict with Russia. Therefore, there is not a single reasonable reason in the interest of our citizens to even consider Moldova's accession to the EU.

Name: Anna Fotyga
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: We acknowledge Moldova as a member of the European community, of a European community of nations that want to realise their aspirations. And we want to help the Moldovan authorities and Moldovan people in achieving candidacy status to the EU as soon as possible.

Name: Emmanuel Maurel
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: I believe it was important for us, as Members of the European Parliament, to reaffirm our support to her at a time when the country is facing immense difficulties and - as it has been said but I repeat - when Moldova's territorial integrity is being questioned, notably by Tiraspol, which has made a completely irresponsible declaration of independence, and by certain Russian leaders who dream of a corridor between Crimea and Transnistria. It is important that we collectively oppose this.

Name: Siegfried Mureșan
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the President of the Republic of Moldova made it very clear to us today: "the citizens of the Republic of Moldova want Moldova to join the European Union, they want to live in safety, stability, with prospects for prosperity, just like the citizens of our countries." And our response, if the citizens of the Republic of Moldova want to join us, must be one and only: "Yes, the Republic of Moldova has a European perspective, the Republic of Moldova can become a member state of the European Union, let's work together to make it happen." In recent months, we have seen how the citizens of the Republic of Moldova have received refugees from Ukraine, in full European spirit...Just as the Moldovan citizens have opened their homes to Ukrainian citizens, we, the European Union, must also open the door to bring the Republic of Moldova closer to the European Union and the prospect of Moldova joining the European Union. Ambitious reforms carried out by the pro-European government in Chișinău are included in the report of our colleague Dragoș Tudorache and detailed in this report. We know that there is much to be done before the moment of accession, but our important message must be "yes, let's get to work."

Name: Tonino Picula
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: We acknowledge many of reforms undertaken, and specify the ones that should remain a priority in the upcoming months and, most notably, the strengthening of the state institutions and justice reform. The European Parliament will remain a strong supporter of all of the reform processes, as confirmed by the Memorandum of Understanding with the Parliament of Moldova last year. We cooperate in many areas, but we should do more and we should increase our financial institutions’ assistance for all of the necessary reforms. Lastly, given the changed security context following the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the pro—European geopolitical orientation, Moldovan efforts should be acknowledged politically too. Supporting a swift assessment of Moldova’s readiness and applications for EU membership would be an essential step in the right direction.

Name: Dacian Cioloş
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The Republic of Moldova is a truly European country, led by a president and a government with a reformist agenda. One third of the citizens of the Republic of Moldova are already European citizens, so the place of the Republic of Moldova is in the European Union, and the signal for accession must come now, when the desire of Moldovans is very clear. History should not be hindered by procedures, and that is why European leaders must be, at least as brave as Maia Sandu. How else should Moldova demonstrate its attachment to European values, when it has risked everything to be part of this family - and you have seen the solidarity that the citizens of the Republic of Moldova have shown towards Ukrainian refugees?...Dear colleagues, let's not ignore the symbolic dimension that granting candidate status to the Republic of Moldova to the European Union can bring. This is a historic moment not only for Eastern Europe but for all of Europe, and we must rise to the occasion of this historic moment that the Republic of Moldova must be part of.

Name: Markéta Gregorová
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: The country certainly needs its reforms improving decentralisation, crucial reforms considering concerning the institutional set—up of the public administration and resilience against state capture. At the same time, the Moldovan Government has been eager to continue to work on its reform, and to have the EU in close integration and sectoral cooperation. The Moldovan citizens spoke, and chose to deepen European relations. We need to support our friends in the Eastern Partnership, and that is why we should highly endorse granting the candidate’s request, based on merit.

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The EU must give clear hope to the Moldovan people, who have voted for the European way and rejected corrupt politicians. Moldova took in refugees from Ukraine and clearly sided with the democratic states, despite the Kremlin threatening Moldova in the same way as it is threatening Ukraine. The people of Moldova deserve to be part of the European family, and the Council should send a clear signal. Moldovans need a European perspective. If we do not seize this opportunity, there may not be another one soon. The EU has the chance to become a real geopolitical actor. A firm hand extended to Moldova would be a step towards it.

Name: Evin Incir
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: at the same time as we see backlash on our fundamental rights in some of our own Member States, we see progress on our European values in countries aspiring for EU membership. Moldova has in recent years taken important steps towards more democracy and respect for the rule of law, even though a lot remains to be done and needs to be intensified as regards judiciary reform and the end of corruption...We need to continue supporting the Moldovan people that has clearly shown that they want to be a part of our Union. My message to all our friends in Moldova is: we stand by you, we support you and we hope to see you represented here in this Parliament soon.

Name: Urmas Paet
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Moldova is in a very difficult situation due to Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, which is why the European Union must give Moldova its full support...At the same time, Moldova is completely dependent on Russia for energy. The EU also must help Moldova increase its energy security by creating new connections. Otherwise, Russia will have a significant leverage to influence Moldova. Moldova’s only power plant is in Russian—controlled Transnistria...It is also important that the EU soon respond positively to Moldova’s application for EU membership.

Name: Ewa Kopacz
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The war in Ukraine, the threat of its escalation, and enormous economic problems are part of everyday life in present-day Moldova. Despite this, Moldova has taken in half a million refugees from Ukraine, half a million in a country with two and a half million inhabitants. Moldova proves every day that it is politically and mentally part of Europe. Its citizens made a choice, they voted for President Maia Sandu, thus expressing their support for Europe. Moldova is a strong link in the Eastern Partnership. I am convinced that in the face of the war in Ukraine, we must pay more attention to stabilizing the entire region. ...Creating a real European perspective for Moldova is not only our moral obligation but also an expression of political common sense.

Name: Maria Grapini
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The presence of President Sandu is also welcome, as she presented her point of view. However, I believe that it is not only important to vote for this accession agreement but also to find a solution to help and support the citizens of the Republic of Moldova, especially now when they face war, have no market for their products, and are dealing with economic and financial problems. Let's expedite the assistance we have proposed, let's support them with procedures and regulations concerning public administration, as President Sandu mentioned that they have a crisis regarding public administration officials. ...We now have a historical duty to support the Republic of Moldova to accelerate its accession and to financially support its citizens.

Name: Bronis Ropė
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: We are indeed pleased to see that this country is working purposefully, having chosen its path, and is striving to create a democratic, secure country and prosperity for its people. Therefore, the European Commission should duly assess Moldova's choice and grant candidate status without delay. This process should not take too long. We should provide the opportunity for Moldova to join the European community quickly.

Name: Eugen Tomac
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Let's not forget something extremely important: Moldova is a victim of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact; it is a former Soviet republic, which, like the Baltic countries, fell victim to criminal agreements. That is why today, through the speech delivered by President Maia Sandu, she emphasized an extremely important issue: the Moldovan people are European. Romanians in Moldova speak an official language of the European Union. A significant portion of Moldova's citizens are already citizens of the European Union, and that is why it is essential to accelerate this process and do justice to the people of Moldova who deserve it.

Name: Andrus Ansip
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Under President Maia Sandu's leadership, Moldova has made significant progress. Moldova's exports have been redirected from the Eastern market to the European Union. In the past year, Moldova has also made substantial progress in media freedom. In one year, it has risen from 89th to 40th place in the World Press Freedom Index. Based on these advancements, I consider it possible to grant Moldova candidate status for the European Union in the near future.

Name: Ilhan Kyuchyuk
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: On the reform agenda, North Macedonia has delivered sustained results. The report recognises the continuous effort to strengthen the rule of law, judicial independence and minority rights, counter corruption, and transparency and political dialogue between government and opposition parties...Having said that, and considering the broader geostrategic context, we are all aware that the postponement of the official start of the accession negotiations is a lose—lose situation – both for North Macedonia and for us, for the EU...In this situation, everyone loses – Bulgaria loses, the Republic of North Macedonia loses, and the European Union loses.

Name: Didier Reynders
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: North Macedonia has demonstrated its commitment to European Union values and determination to advance on its EU path. The country has condemned Russia’s military aggression and expressed its firm support to Ukraine and its people. The country is also fully aligned with all the European Union’s declarations, statements and restrictive measures on Russia. At the same time, the country continues to show its determination to advance on EU reforms. As you have rightly pointed out in your report, North Macedonia has maintained a steady pace of progress in the implementation of reforms, in particular in key areas such as the judiciary, the fight against corruption and organised crime...To conclude, it is important that North Macedonia continue to deliver on reforms and that the EU deliver in return. The official launch of accession negotiations through the first Intergovernmental Conference will be the strongest possible signal the EU could send to the country, to the region and beyond. // North Macedonia belongs in the European Union, and the official launch of accession negotiations provides the best guarantees to ensure that the rule of law, fundamental rights and European values are implemented in practice in the interests of all citizens.

Name: Christian Sagartz
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: It is bad news because North Macedonia has made and implemented profound reforms in many areas. I am not talking about simple legislative decisions – they have gone as far as changing their constitution and even their country's name...The European Union and Europe as a whole are losing credibility in the Western Balkans if we do not send strong signals. This loss of credibility is precisely what leads others to exploit this political vacuum: Russia, China – others will come and make offers, and then it is in our hands – also due to the impact of the COVID pandemic – to act quickly. The impressive signal of unity after Putin's attack on Ukraine must overflow into united action in the Western Balkans. We need these states. We need these states by our side, we need them within the European Union.

Name: Christian Sagartz
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The European Union and Europe as a whole are losing credibility in the Western Balkans if we do not send strong signals. This loss of credibility is precisely what leads others to exploit this political vacuum: Russia, China – others will come and make offers, and then it is in our hands – also due to the impact of the COVID pandemic – to act quickly. The impressive signal of unity after Putin's attack on Ukraine must overflow into united action in the Western Balkans. We need these states. We need these states by our side, we need them within the European Union.

Name: Tonino Picula
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: They underwent substantial reforms, including to strengthening its democracy and fighting against corruption, and even changing their name. And contrary to some others, North Macedonia has fully aligned with the European Union sanctions against Russia. There must be no excuses for further delay if we want to preserve our credibility...Given the changed geopolitical context of the Russian aggression on Ukraine, strengthening the enlargement policy is more important than ever.

Name: Tineke Strik
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: They are waiting now for over ten years for the accession talks to start, while having fulfilled the conditions. Until now, the citizens supported brave pro—EU leaders...Putin’s aggression in Ukraine rings another alarm bell. Russian influence is still rising at our doorstep in the Western Balkans. We can make democracy win from autocracy if we practice what we preach.

Name: Anna Bonfrisco
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: North Macedonia confirms its position in the liberal and democratic tradition of the European Union and NATO, of which it has been an active member since 2020. Furthermore, it aligns with the EU's foreign and security policy, even against the unjustified and illegal Russian aggression...We strongly hope for the continuation of bilateral dialogue with Bulgaria to finally promote the necessary national reforms for full cooperation within the European framework, especially concerning minority issues. This is a historic moment to demonstrate the common will to converge towards a single, strong European family, carrying the values of freedom and democracy...North Macedonia represents a geostrategic investment in favor of peace, stability, and growth for the entire European continent; Europe must rise to this mission.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Dear colleagues, you want North Macedonia to start negotiations with the European Union. Wonderful. This can happen tomorrow, colleagues, tomorrow. For that, it is only necessary to change the Constitution this evening, to ban the language of hatred, to stop the humiliation of Bulgarian history, and to resolve all these issues...Because what is happening now, the pressure, the unfair pressure on Bulgarian society and memory is repelling Bulgarians, disappointing them, and making them very eurosceptic. In practice, this pressure on Bulgaria works for Putin and the Russian column in Bulgaria and the European Union. Is this what you want to achieve? // The Copenhagen criteria are the basis of the so-called "European values." Quote: Mr. Erdogan, stop holding Finland and Sweden's NATO membership requests hostage. These requests are legitimate, but your blackmail is not. Mr. President, stop believing that Turkey has the right to act as it pleases in Syria. You are undermining the fight against Daesh, a terrorism that has caused grief on our continent. Mr. Erdogan, respect the sovereignty of Greece and Cyprus, as it is not negotiable. Mr. President, do not buy the wheat that Russia is stealing from the Ukrainians, and do not welcome oligarchs with open arms. The war in Ukraine is a historic turning point. This time, it is up to you, for once, to put Turkey on the right side of history. You still have the opportunity, but time is running out.

Name: Gwendoline Delbos-Corfield
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: This report highlights that our approach so far has failed to seriously address the human rights crisis in Turkey that is becoming extremely dire alongside the erosion of democracy and the rule of law...Generalised discrimination of minorities continues, while the European Commission continues to engage in high—level dialogues. Of course, it is a step in the right direction that the EU—Turkey Joint Parliamentary Committee took place earlier this year. But this report shows that we urgently need a much more severe attitude that can no longer be based on mutual trust.

Name: Dimitrios Papadimoulis
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: The anti-democratic regression, the historical revisionism, and the aggression of Erdogan's leadership towards Greece and Cyprus are distancing Turkey further away from democracy, international law, and the European Union. They are turning it into a destabilizing factor and an unreliable and dangerous partner. We see this in how Turkey behaves towards the Russian invasion of Ukraine and towards the requests of Finland and Sweden. Ladies and gentlemen, if we want peace and stability in the region and democracy in Turkey, we need a stricter stance towards the Turkish leadership, greater pressure, not a policy of equal distances, not tea and sympathy.

Name: Stelios Koumpouroulis
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Turkey, for example, intensifies its aggression against Greece, challenging the sovereignty of Greek islands in the Aegean, pursues an aggressive policy in Cyprus with the opening of Varosha, violating UN resolutions, accuses Sweden and Finland of ties with terrorism, destabilizes Libya and Syria, disregards the destruction of Hagia Sophia, which it turned into a mosque, and suppresses the religious freedoms of minorities. The European Union began negotiations with the Turkish Republic, but now, it is in dialogue with an imitation of the Ottoman Empire. Respecting its principles and values, the European Union must keep the accession negotiations frozen until Turkey comprehends the democratic and substantial changes it needs to make in its government.

Name: Hilde Vautmans
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: there is no place in Europe for this Turkey, where journalists are attacked, opposition members are suppressed, and violence against women seems to be tolerated, and where binding rulings of the European Court of Human Rights are ignored. No membership, but a partnership. Turkey is an important strategic partner, as has become even clearer during the war in Ukraine. However, this does not mean that Europe should abandon its values.

Name: Lucas Fourlas
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I don't know how hypocritical it is to talk about a report that includes the words "Turkey" and "progress" in the same proposal. I don't know how useful it is to keep listing all those arguments from this platform that clearly demonstrate that Erdogan's Turkey has nothing to do with the European project. Even if some have their ears closed, we must stand here, before you, and remind you of some bitter realities. We owe it to the millions of victims of Turkish expansion, to the Greeks, Pontians, Armenians, and Kurds. I owe it to the dead and refugees of my homeland, Cyprus. All of them are looking into our eyes today and asking - asking you, Mr. Commissioner - how much longer we will pretend that Turkey has a place next to democratic European societies...If there were an answer, and if we were serving values and not interests, we wouldn't even be discussing a progress report on Turkey today.

Name: Nikos Androulakis
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Mr. Erdogan has been demanding the demilitarization of the Greek islands in the Eastern Aegean, directly challenging Greece's sovereignty. He continues provocations in the Eastern Mediterranean and engages in illegal actions in the enclosed area of Varosha, disregarding UN decisions. He blackmails Europe concerning Finland and Sweden's entry into NATO, while being the only country that has not imposed sanctions on Russia. He continues to violate human rights within Turkey, with anyone challenging his authority being directly labeled as an enemy of the state or a terrorist

Name: Georgios Kyrtsos
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: we must prioritize the defense of the rights of the Kurds. Erdogan attacks or has occupied areas of the Kurds in Syria and Iraq. He does not respect international legality and may engage in adventures against Greece and Cyprus...Through a mix of prosecutions and regulations, he seeks to remove the Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP) from parliament. Erdogan's mistreatment of the Kurds and Turkey's system of power should play a fundamental role in our evaluation of Turkey and the prospects of Euro-Turkish relations

Name: Anna-Michelle Asimakopoulou
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Turkey cannot continue to threaten, provoke, and blackmail. We must not show any more tolerance. Turkey cannot always be the "naughty child" we tolerate, tolerate its behavior, and try to reprimand. Ladies and gentlemen, my country, Greece, in the face of escalating Turkish provocations, is doing its duty towards both Europe and its southern borders. It is the right time for Europe to do its duty towards Greece and say with actions, "Enough is enough."

Name: Dimitris Papadakis
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: luckily, we have the strategic partner called Turkey, which aligns with sanctions against Russia, does not welcome Russian oligarchs, and does not engage in Eastern bazaars. Luckily, Turkey does not blackmail with migration and does not instrumentalize refugees. Fortunately, Turkey respects the human rights of its citizens and does not imprison anyone who disagrees. It has good relations with its neighbors and does not provoke tensions every now and then. It does not occupy European territories by force, does not provoke in the Aegean, and is not attempting a new invasion in Syria as we speak. Unfortunately for us, this is a fairytale that we would very much like to be true, but like all fairytales, it has an end.

Name: Lefteris Christoforou
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I have a strong conviction and demand that the European Parliament's report on Turkey should start and end with a strong, clear, and strict message: that the European Union does not tolerate any invader, that the European Union cannot and should not have any relation with any invader, especially the invader of invaders, who has occupied European territory of a member state of the European Union, Cyprus, for 48 years, flagrantly violates human rights and the rule of law, continues to threaten and violate the sovereign rights of EU member countries, Cyprus and Greece, and does not respect any principle or value of the European Union. On these issues, the European Union must be uncompromising.

Name: Elizabeth Vozemberg-Vryonides
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the revisionist stance of Turkey, President Erdogan's threats and blackmail, have exceeded all limits. Recently, the conscious escalation of tension, the offensive reference of Erdogan to the Greek Prime Minister, the blackmailing dilemmas, and the contempt for international law call us to rise to the occasion. Daily violations and overflights over Greek territory are followed by Erdogan's threats, as of yesterday, against those who, if possible, left the islands to Greece and allowed Cyprus to join the European Union. It has come to the point of threatening a new invasion in the Aegean and a repetition of 1922...A European Union with double standards is not conceivable; it would undermine our historical responsibility towards European citizens and the democratic ethical values of the Union.

Name: Kostas Mavridis
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The neo-Ottoman expansion has brought us to this point, with security issues for the states of the Eastern Mediterranean, particularly Greece and Cyprus, as well as other countries such as Syria, Libya, and even the Caucasus, all for one reason: we followed the policy of appeasement, which unfortunately feeds the beast. Turkey's regime brutally violates both human rights and international law. We have been counting the days since Russia's brutal invasion of Ukraine, but in the case of Cyprus, which constitutes EU territory, we have been counting years

Name: Billy Kelleher
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: I wish this report could read differently, but it does indicate how Turkey has backslid in the fundamental principles of democracy...The report goes on and goes on. It does highlight, unfortunately, and expresses deep concern about the state—sponsored deterioration in human rights situation for the LGBTQI people, in particular with regard to physical attacks and hate crimes, especially against transgender persons and protective bans on pride marches across the country. I would love to see a different Turkey, but we have a long way to go before it is acceptable to the norms and principles which we prescribe in this particular Parliament.

Name: Clare Daly
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: year on year, we hear the same rhetoric about Turkey’s inability to live up to European values and standards. And yet, at the same time, we’re really happy to give them billions on a filthy deal designed to ensure that those fleeing what were often Western-provoked wars in Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria and so on are prevented from exercising their legal right to seek asylum in Europe and kept in Turkey.

Name: Eugen Tomac
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I would have liked this report to highlight the positive aspects of the relationship between the European Union and Turkey, but it seems that the aspects that bring us closer to Turkey are increasingly missing. That is why I believe it is essential to exert the necessary pressure on Ankara, so that it does not drift further away from the European Union...In the current security context, generated by Russia's illegal invasion of Ukraine, we must do everything in our power to keep Turkey on our side, because a Turkey even more vulnerable than it is today, which unfortunately tramples on democracy and disregards human rights, does not help us in any way. That is why I believe the Commission must insist on this approach, to keep Turkey as close as possible.

Name: Mick Wallace
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: Turkey is a NATO member and is a partner of many EU Member States. So why does the EU actually tolerate what Turkey gets up to? Turkey has been breaking international law on a regular basis for a long time and we put up with it. Now we complain, and rightly so, about their illegality with Cyprus and Greece. But you know what? I actually think Turkey must be confused because we never said bugger all to them about their illegal occupation of Iraq or their stealing oil, their illegal occupation of Syria, along with the Americans and the Israelis, where oil and food has been stolen.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: another report on Turkey that clearly shows the absurd, fearful, and toothless European foreign policy. A country led by dictator Erdogan has no place in the European Union. Moreover, it is not a reliable partner, not a strategic partner, not our friend. On the contrary, Turkey is an aggressive state, where the idea of restoring the Ottoman Empire prevails, and if you continue to close your eyes, it is very bad. Perhaps you have missed it, but Erdogan categorically opposed the acceptance of Sweden and Finland into NATO. At the same time, Turkey continues to actively cooperate with Russia. Do you still consider this state an ally and a partner?

Name: Sirpa Pietikäinen
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: As a critical NATO member and a neighboring country to the EU, Turkey is drifting further away from EU accession criteria and common values. It is not in the EU's interest to have such a country as our neighbor. Turkey plays a central role, for example, in EU refugee policy, and the current situation is not sustainable. In the EU, we must do everything we can to strengthen Turkey's democratic development. Officially, Turkey's EU membership process is still ongoing, although it has been practically frozen for years. Turkey has systematically failed to implement its commitments related to the accession negotiations. Turkey's human rights situation is also deteriorating, and Parliament should condemn the pressure on civil society and human rights defenders in Turkey.

Name: Clément Beaune
Type: Member of Council of the EU
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Ukraine is part of our European family, without any hesitation...Let us be very clear, I believe and hope that we will be able to reach a consensus at this European summit to send the expected signal of granting candidacy, which should not be confused with immediate accession.

Name: Clément Beaune
Type: Member of Council of the EU
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Georgia has shown a very clear European intention, and the recognition of a perspective is probably necessary.

Name: Clément Beaune
Type: Member of Council of the EU
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: We need to reaffirm that the swiftest possible accession of the Western Balkans countries is necessary, but, as I mentioned earlier, it is also essential that they align with European Union values, particularly with regards to our sanctions policies that reflect these values.

Name: Ursula von der Leyen
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: The opinion we presented last week recognises Ukraine’s aspirations. It acknowledges the immense progress that Ukraine’s democracy has achieved since the Maidan. Our opinion stems from a careful and thorough assessment of the reality on the ground. And this evidence tells us that Ukraine, in the opinion of the Commission, deserves a European perspective, it deserves candidate status, of course on the understanding that the country will carry out a number of further, important reforms...we know that approximately 70% of all EU standards and norms have already been adopted by Ukraine...Ukraine is a very robust parliamentary democracy with a well-functioning administration. The administrative reform and decentralization have been successful, which is evident in our close cooperation with Ukraine...But, in the end, all these achievements are made possible because the people of Ukraine carry Europe in their minds and, above all, in their hearts.

Name: Ursula von der Leyen
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Moldova has taken decisive steps towards Europe too, with a very clear mandate from its citizens. It is on a real pro—reform, anti—corruption and European path for the very first time since independence. And this is why it deserves a European perspective and European candidate status, again on the understanding that the country will carry out a number of further important reforms. In particular, its economy and public administration require major reforms and efforts. But provided that the country’s leaders stay the course – and I have no doubt about that – we believe that the country has the potential to live up to these requirements.

Name: Ursula von der Leyen
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Its application has strength, in particular the market orientation of its economy, with a strong private sector. To succeed, however, the country must now come together politically. It must design a clear path towards structural reforms and towards the European Union, a path that concretely sets out the necessary reforms, brings civil society on board, and benefits from broad political support. And this is why we recommend to the Council to grant Georgia the European perspective, but to come back and assess how the country meets a number of conditions before granting it candidate status.

Name: Ursula von der Leyen
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: The whole history of our European Union is one of young democracies getting stronger together...It is the long path of reconciliation in the Western Balkans and, I believe, a path that must lead all six Western Balkan countries to join our European Union.

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Granting EU candidate status to Ukraine is so widely supported...I call on some EU Member States’ politicians to stop sending pessimistic messages to the struggling Ukraine by saying that Ukraine’s path to EU membership will take decades. Show your leadership so that this country becomes part of our family as soon as possible. The impression is that it is not Ukraine but the politicians of some EU countries not ready for Ukraine’s membership

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I sincerely congratulate Moldova. I visited the country last week. They have performed a miracle when in peaceful democratic elections they managed to overcome the Kremlin’s candidate. They have turned their country back towards Europe. We must help Moldova seize this historic opportunity.

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: On Monday, with the largest demonstration in the history of modern Georgia, the people sent us a signal from Tbilisi that they are determined to follow the path of Europe. I say very clearly, we are with you Georgians. Unfortunately, it seems that Georgia’s Government did its best not to make the European Commission recommendation more favorable to Georgia. I appeal to all Georgian politicians – both the ruling elites and the opposition – find the strength for a strong European agenda. Your amazing people deserve it. Releasing the imprisoned two former presidents and owner of the opposition media would be an important step towards a European way of life

Name: Iratxe García Pérez
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The prospect of enlargement is undoubtedly the most successful foreign policy of our Union because the horizon of integration is the only vaccine to overcome historical resentments between our countries and communities, to prevent wars, and to promote peace...We must fulfill our promises and send a clear message: the future of the Western Balkans is in the European Union. Ukraine, the Republic of Moldova, and Georgia as well. Our commitment is clear. The path is long, but it is worth it. And you must also address the necessary reforms in all areas. In the area of the rule of law, of course, but you must also strengthen the role of civil society and social partners.

Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Madam President, granting candidate status to Ukraine is a just recognition of the Ukrainian people's sacrifice for our European values. We could not ignore – as I have reiterated many times in this hemicycle – the bloodshed in the name of the ideals of peace, democracy, and sovereignty in this unjust war. I hope that the same sense of responsibility will also guide the members of the Council on the issue of the Western Balkans. We also have a duty to pave the European path for these nations. This is the position of my group, which is also in favor of granting candidate status to Moldova.

Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: I’m happy that the Commission has taken the historical decision to propose the status of an accession candidate for Ukraine and Moldova, as called for by this House, and I hope that the Council will also decide accordingly. The war Russia is raging against Ukraine, is also one against European values and is also one against European integration. And as a European family, we need to stand together. Ukraine and Moldova have made important steps and reforms, notably against corruption. Not all is well – much remains to be done – but the progress is there and it will be given new impetus also with a candidate status.

Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Georgia, too, has European ambition that we want to support. And I would strongly encourage the Georgian Government not to undermine the country’s past progress and to go forward making the necessary reforms.

Name: Ska Keller
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Apart from those three countries, we also need to see a clear commitment and perspective for the Western Balkans. These countries have all been waiting for years for any sort of progress in their accession perspective. Many have made enormous reforms – North Macedonia even changed its name – but are still being held in limbo and this must finally come to an end. We need a clear and reliable path to the EU for the Western Balkans for their own sake, but also for the growth and the strength of our Union.

Name: Marco Zanni
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: the phase we are facing at this moment is delicate, not only for the political and symbolic significance that some decisions will have – we hope that there will be a unanimous decision to grant candidate status to Ukraine

Name: Raffaele Fitto
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: I believe it is important to reaffirm, even on this occasion, our clear and full support for Ukraine. But to do this, I think it is also important, in these hours, to carefully read Putin's not casual statements, where he clearly indicates what his idea of the future is, that of proposing the borders that traditionally belonged to the Soviet domain in the past. This is why we must support Ukraine's status. For this reason, with the rules that you rightly emphasized, we must express clear and strong support also for Georgia and Moldova, as it is crucial for this to happen.

Name: Manon Aubry
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: The return of war to our doorstep and the tragedy suffered by the Ukrainians have brought up the question of their accession to European integration in our debates, and that is legitimate. The call from President Zelensky and the Ukrainian people in this regard should and must be heard. The prospect of closer ties between Ukraine and the European Union is a powerful political symbol in this unique context. We needed and still need to demonstrate concrete solidarity with the Ukrainians. But let's be honest, we also owe them transparency, respect, and honesty. Ukraine is currently a country at war. Its institutions are still fragile, and its standard of living is far from the levels of the rest of the European Union. So, as we have always said, enlargement can make sense for Ukraine, as well as for other countries in our European continent. But it must always be done with a goal of upward harmonization, so that all European peoples benefit from both social and democratic progress...the path to accession is still long. I want to reiterate to the Ukrainians that the European Union stands by your side. Our destinies are intertwined. Accession is a path that must be seriously explored, without false promises.

Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)

Quote: Europeans have every reason to be proud of and confident in the project of a united Europe, guaranteeing peace, security and prosperity. Our Eastern partners – Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia – have chosen and proven that they deserve the European path. We must now walk this path together and finally consolidate the victory of liberal democracy over Eastern totalitarianism. I firmly believe that an independent and democratic Belarus will repeat its march towards Europe as well. The historic decision to grant EU candidate status to Ukraine and Moldova and to encourage Georgia to continue on its path will reinforce the EU’s status as an important geopolitical player.

Name: Viola Von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: The future of this continent is to be reshaped, either according to our values or to Putin’s rules. Therefore, it is high time that the EU starts speaking in the language of power and demonstrates its firmness and geopolitical credibility. We also have long-standing commitments towards the Western Balkan states. Europe won’t be complete unless we deliver the concrete steps now regarding the promise of their European integration. I call on all European leaders to take political responsibility and shape the Europe of tomorrow, where the Western Balkans, as well as Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia, have a place.

Name: Jaak Madison
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: But at the same time, I absolutely understand Ukrainians who really are willing to move closer to the EU. If Ukraine is really dreaming and really wanting to have candidate status, I think there is no question: of course, we have to give it. Absolutely. I think there is likely an absolutely majority in the House also here who agrees on this. I’ve told, several times also, the Ukrainians that the main goal can’t be just to be a member of the EU. The main point is to really be a successful country with a functional economy, with less corruption and to really move on the right way. Then, of course, it can be also in years, membership to the EU. There’s no doubt of this.

Name: Beata Szydło
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Tomorrow, the European Council must send a clear and very distinct signal that Ukraine, Moldova, and Georgia are candidates for the European Union. Ukraine needs the European Union, but the European Union also needs Ukraine and all these countries, including the Western Balkan countries, to become members of our Community. If they are in the European Union, they will not be in Putin's sphere of influence. The war in Ukraine and the heroic struggle of Ukrainians are also fought in our name, on behalf of all of us Europeans. We must be aware that Ukrainians are fighting today for our freedom and sovereignty, and they must receive a clear and solidary message. We all must be united; we must support them militarily, humanitarianly, and economically. It is our duty towards the future of Europe, towards the future of our nations, all of us.

Name: Kinga Gál
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: We support the candidate status of Ukraine, Moldova, and Georgia, as well as the accelerated European integration of the Western Balkan countries. In this period full of war challenges, this is a good opportunity to promote European unity and strengthen these countries. Of course, every country must meet the accession criteria, including the Copenhagen criteria. The candidate status of countries should be considered under the same values and conditions. Therefore, while supporting the candidate status of Ukraine and Moldova, Georgia and Bosnia and Herzegovina should also be granted candidate status simultaneously...The credibility of the Union also depends on the acceleration of the accession process of the Western Balkan countries, as in this geopolitical situation, the security and stability of the region are of fundamental interest to the Union. For this, it is necessary to advance the accession negotiations with Serbia and Montenegro, to start the negotiations with North Macedonia and Albania, and to provide visa liberalization for Kosovo. We need to give new momentum to enlargement.

Name: Tineke Strik
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: the Russian aggression has increased the urgency to pull our neighbouring countries closer to us, to protect them against destructive influence and help them in building democratic and free countries. And the candidate status amplifies our cooperation, if combined with active support. We applaud this step towards Ukraine and Moldova but, at the same time, we need really urgently to give perspective to the citizens of the Western Balkans. North Macedonia and Albania are waiting too long, having fulfilled all the criteria and trust in the EU is now really at stake. Kosovo deserves visa liberalisation and the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina need a credible promise that they will get candidate status if their political leaders are willing to show commitment and take the necessary steps. We need to offer perspective now. This is needed for geopolitical unity, but also desperately needed to offer the citizens the safeguards of security, economic prospects and European values.

Quote: after more than two years of working on Bosnia and Herzegovina, I can conclude that our European engagement in BiH is neither geopolitical nor strategic.
