While NATO clearly and unequivocally defines the strategic importance of BiH for the security and stability not only of the Western Balkans but of the entire Europe, we, as Europeans, stumble through a forest of various interests that have largely poisoned or prevented unified European action in Bos-nia and Herzegovina...What BiH needs now, in addition to candidate country status, is a clear and decisive Europe-an intervention. BiH needs unified European mediation in establishing the rule of law, fighting corruption and organized crime, ensuring an independent judiciary, and securing free media. The EU must decisively interrupt the cat-and-mouse games we play with different local politicians through a clear framework of conditionality in the enlargement methodology.

Name: Tineke Strik
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: With this report, the Parliament makes very clear that the future of Bosnia is in the EU and it urges for a serious revival of the EU enlargement agenda. The Russian aggression has made this integration process even more urgent, as destabili-sation of the region is a real threat. But we are also frank: for Bosnia to advance on its path to the EU, commitment is needed from both sides...HDZ cannot insist on cementing ethnic division through a discriminatory electoral law which undermines the principle of one person, one vote. Leaders need to overcome the past and implement the highly needed reforms transforming Bosnia into the functional, multi-ethnic state that the citizens so much want and deserve.

Name: Bernhard Zimniok
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: Bosnia and Herzegovina has received around 1.5 billion euros in aid and support from the EU alone until 2020. Recently, there were additional 250 million euros in COVID assistance. The condition for this aid is primarily the strengthening of democracy and combating corruption. In 2007, Bosnia ranked 84th in the Corruption Perceptions Index. After receiving billions in aid, the country now ranks 110th. Just like in the case of Greece, Bosnia can do whatever it wants. The funds will be transferred anyway, and as a reward, they now want to bring the country into the EU, despite its high level of corruption, its lack of action against uncon-trolled mass migration through its territory to the EU, and the fact that it would be a net recipient for decades.

Name: Assita Kanko
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: In today's modified European security framework, the ECR Group advocates for a peaceful Western Balkans region that can continue on the European path without Russian interfer-ence. We welcome the political agreement of June 12 on the principles for ensuring a func-tional Bosnia and Herzegovina, which is essential for the stability of that country.

Name: Fabio Massimo Castaldo
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: For this reason, the Council’s readiness to grant candidate status to Bosnia is a very im-portant step as we cannot risk further disenchantment and we cannot give the impression that we are leaving the Western Balkans behind. The implementation of the commitments, as set out in the political agreement reached on 12 June 2022, will be paramount and I strongly hope that after the Commission reports on the 14 key priorities, as requested by the Council, we’ll swiftly welcome Bosnia Herzegovina as an official candidate. Dear colleagues, delaying further the inevitable EU perspective for the Balkans in the EU is like playing with fire as there is a concrete risk that they will look elsewhere.

Name: Sunčana Glavak
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: strengthening media pluralism in all languages in Bosnia and Herzegovina, calling for in-creased cross-border cooperation in the fight against crime, and ensuring the European per-spective for Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, I want to reiterate once again: Bosnia and Herzegovina must remain united, terri-torially intact, with equal rights for its three constituent peoples. I also condemn any disre-gard for international and national norms and obligations, as well as any destabilization in the country. This must be a strong message. On the other hand, the politics of Bosnia and Herzegovina must finalize constitutional and electoral reforms and progress on its European path, being aware that it requires substantial transformation...It is especially important for us Croats and the Croatian government, and also for us Europe-ans. Bosnia and Herzegovina is a European country, our neighboring country, and half a mil-lion Croats live there. The message to Bosnia and Herzegovina is also that it should engage in constitutional and electoral law reform, so that this key prerequisite that we often mention can be completed in the best possible way before the elections in October. I will conclude: challenges, opportunities, and solutions - yes, but not just opportunities. We must offer Bosnia and Herzegovina a solution because it is a security priority for Europe.

Name: Andreas Schieder
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: the last good year of Bosnia-Herzegovina’s path towards the European Union, on its Europe-an path, was 2016, when Bosnia submitted its candidacy application for the membership in the European Union; six years ago...But it’s up to the Commission to submit also its evaluation as soon as possible, and it’s on the other side up to Bosnia-Herzegovina to finally fulfil the main part of this obligation. But in order to succeed in doing so, it takes also a significant change in the behaviour of the po-litical leaders in Bosnia-Herzegovina, especially of the leaders of the specific entities, to overcome divisions and to work towards a European future.

Name: Romeo Franz
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: We all agree that the sustainable stabilization of Bosnia and Herzegovina is in the European interest, especially in light of the Russian aggression in Ukraine. We know that Putin wants to expand his influence in the Western Balkans and in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Therefore, it is necessary for the European Union, together with our international allies, to fulfill our re-sponsibility and ensure peace and stability. At the same time, efforts on the Bosnian side must be increased to obtain candidate status for the EU, as they are essential for the de-mocratization process in the country.

Name: Balázs Hidvéghi
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: The EU should stabilise and pacify the region, and a real prospect of EU membership can do that. However, the proposition of sanctions, for instance, against elected leaders, leads no-where...Moreover, Bosnia Herzegovina lies exactly on the Balkan migration route. Therefore, its inte-gration into the EU with enforced border protection would contribute to stability for the local people as well as for Europe as a whole. We cannot waste any more opportunities. The EU must give membership—candidate status to Bosnia—Herzegovina now.

Name: Delara Burkhardt
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: We see how Russian, but also Chinese influence destabilizes the region. And in Bosnia and Herzegovina, we see how an ethnonationalist boycotts and divides, how minorities are per-secuted, and hard-fought progress is under pressure. It is now up to the EU to show solidari-ty with the democratic forces in the country, to push for the elections in October to take place, and to ensure they are free and fair...My appeal to the Commission: Do not allow enlargement policy to remain a pawn of mem-ber state interests, but ensure that it becomes a powerful geopolitical tool. You too - there is much work to be done in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but you also have it in your hands to make the EU not only a hope but a promise for a better future for the people in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Name: Joachim Stanisław Brudziński
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: I think we all agree that there will be no safe, stable Europe without safe and stable states in the Western Balkans region. That is why Poland actively supports the European aspira-tions of these countries and therefore expresses unconditional support for the unity of Bos-nia and Herzegovina.

Name: Vladimír Bilčík
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: We are committed to Serbia’s European Union accession. This is very clear and it is stated in the first paragraph of the report...As the European Parliament reiterates its support for Serbia’s EU membership, it also recalls that a credible enlargement perspective requires political will, sustainable efforts and irreversible reforms in all areas, particularly those linked to the rule of law, as well as unwavering commitment to European standards and values. How do we measure the accession pace? The report reiterates that the progress on the rule of law and fundamental rights chapters, full alignment with EU foreign security and defence policy, including sanctions against Russia, as well as the normalisation of Serbia’s relations with Kosovo, will determine the pace of accession...Certain open issues remain as open as they were at the opening of the accession negotiations. This regards improving electoral conditions, fight against corruption and organised crime, improving media environment, and repeated calls for cross—party consensus on EU—related reforms for ensuring the country’s progress on its EU path...EU accession is Serbia’s strategic priority and it is Serbia’s strategic decision. So we need to see it treated strategically by political leadership in Serbia. It is therefore important to start moving towards the EU, not sideways. // I would like to thank those who see Serbia as a strategically important partner in the Western Balkans, and who understand that Serbia’s successful EU path is more important now than ever...Third point, when I look at the past 100 years of Serbian history, I certainly do not see Russia as playing a dominant role. I hope that all the relevant pro-European and Serbian political forces can discover and rediscover this part of their history and base their decisions on this when looking to the future.

Name: Janez Lenarčič
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: There have been significant improvements, including those that allowed the participation of all political forces. But the challenges remain. Therefore, the work needs to continue to further strengthen the functioning of democratic institutions...The progress made by Serbia on EU-related reforms has allowed us to open, last December for the first time, a cluster of four chapters on the green agenda and sustainable connectivity...However, reforms need to continue. Building on the momentum of last December and on the successful January referendum on the constitutional amendments, we expect Serbia to deliver real and tangible results, in particular in the area of the rule of law and on dialogue with Pristina...In the current geopolitical context, Serbia has demonstrated its commitment to EU values by aligning with the number of EU declarations and by supporting relevant UN General Assembly resolutions on Ukraine. We now expect Serbia to continue to show this commitment and step up its efforts in progressively aligning with the EU Common Foreign and Security Policy, including declarations and restrictive measures in line with the EU-Serbia negotiating framework. // We count on Serbia, as a sincere European partner to stand with us and our common values, security and prosperity. On the Commission side, we will continue to do all we can to speed up Serbia’s pace of negotiations

Name: Janez Lenarčič
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: We are facing unprecedented challenges in Europe that make it clear that EU membership is the most important and most reliable tool for peace, stability and long-term prosperity.

Name: Dimitris Papadakis
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Serbia is part of Europe, and its future inevitably lies in becoming a full member of the European Union. However, there is already significant delay in this process, unfortunately caused by the country's own government. Reforms are lagging, social justice is absent, respect for differing opinions is lacking, and journalists and media that are not controlled by the government face censorship. There is also inertia in addressing extreme and inhumane exploitation of foreign labor. Attacks on opposition leaders by paramilitary groups are occurring. When aspiring to be part of European principles and values, Serbia must align itself with them and join in imposing sanctions against Russia, without much talk.

Name: Klemen Grošelj
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The progress report or rather the lack of progress report on Serbia's EU accession that is before us unfortunately does not tell the whole story of a country that somehow cannot or does not want to make the necessary political effort to definitively choose the European path...If Serbia does not wish to remain perpetually a candidate country, it must decisively embark on a path of deep reforms in the rule of law, fundamental democratic standards, independence of the judiciary and media, functioning of civil society, and other fundamental values and principles that the EU is based on. Mere formal compliance with commitments is no longer sufficient; genuine implementation of all reforms for the benefit of Serbian citizens is needed, and only then can conditions for accession to the European Union be met.

Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: despite all efforts of the European Parliament, Serbia is not much more democratic than it was after the 2020 election boycott. It is a country that still lacks genuine democratic plurality, media freedoms and political culture, which will prepare it for the EU...I would like to remind President Vučić about the utmost need to align with Europe on our common stance. I truly believe that the Russian invasion of Ukraine is a watershed moment in modern Europe. The EU expects from the new government full alignment in terms of foreign policy and introduction of sanctions against Russia.

Name: Susanna Ceccardi
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: if we look at a map, the enlargement to the Balkans appears as an inevitable matter from a geopolitical perspective. However, the Balkans Summit on 23 June was a failure. None of the candidate countries has seen substantial progress, and there is great disappointment among all leaders as the European Union has failed to fulfill its promises to the Western Balkans. The question arises: in which direction is European foreign policy heading? We are opening up to the enlargement of two nations like Ukraine and Moldova to the East, but we have not paid enough attention to what is happening in our own neighborhood. Leaving a void at the borders of our space, if not within it, inevitably leaves room for other actors.

Name: Emmanuel Maurel
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: does the Parliament really want to encourage Serbia to join the European Union? Sometimes, when I hear our debates or read our texts, I start to doubt it, because they are systematically biased, without nuances – nuances that we show when it comes to other countries in the Western Balkans. We criticize Belgrade, make demands that are untenable, continue to ignore the weight of history, misunderstand the country's political culture, and above all, disregard the progress made. Of course, the situation is not satisfactory. We have mentioned corruption, hindered civil society, and media issues. But progress has been made following our recommendations.

Name: Andor Deli
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: The report before us should be about how the European Parliament will help Serbia become a member of the Union as soon as possible, but instead, the report tends to lecture, prescribe, and contains unacceptable exaggerations that only further hinder the country's accession process, question the EU's credibility, and alienate Serbian citizens. This is contrary to the strategic interests of both Serbia and the EU. It is incredible that when we see a war raging in a country neighboring the EU, some fail to see that Serbia's accession would strengthen the stability of the Union.

Name: Eugen Tomac
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I believe that Serbia must understand that there are no double standards when you embark on the path of EU accession. In this context, it is essential for Serbia's policies to demonstrate through actions that they align with European standards, and they must apply the sanctions we have applied to Russia precisely because this war has given us a new reality, allowing us to understand that only united, only together, can we face all challenges.

Name: Alessandra Moretti
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: We understand the difficulties and peculiarities of historical reasons, we appreciate the efforts already made on reforms, as well as the commitment to welcome Ukrainian refugees, but it is not enough. We ask the Serbian authorities to have courage and to stand unequivocally on the side of the Ukrainian people, invaded without justifiable reason and violated in its sovereignty. This also means defending European values of democracy and freedom against Russian propaganda, which continues to infiltrate Serbian media to subtly influence public opinion. Finally, I invite the Serbian government to have the courage to reach an agreement that achieves full normalization of relations with neighboring countries, a crucial step to accelerate on the European path. Take courage, and Europe will be by your side to support you.

Name: Georgios Kyrtsos
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: we want Serbia in the European Union. We believe that we have a common European perspective. But we must say that now is not the time for discounts on principles and strategic issues. Serbia's leadership, unfortunately, turns a blind eye to Russia at a time when there is a war in Ukraine, with Putin's responsibility destabilizing the whole of Europe...Furthermore, there is Russian influence and destabilization in the Western Balkans. And when we talk about Serbia, we are talking about enlargement towards the Western Balkans. There is also a tendency for Russia to lean on China to cope with international pressure, and we also have Serbia encouraging relations with both Russia and China. I believe that, with this mix, Serbia cannot hope for rapid and positive developments concerning the European Union.

Name: Željana Zovko
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the countries in the Western Balkans need a sincere and credible European perspective. From their side, the enlargement countries should show their willingness to adhere to European values, standards and principles. Serbia has made considerable progress on its reform agenda, but still has not delivered on a few critical aspects. While facing the security threats in the east of Europe, it should be clear that no further integration can happen without clear alignment with our common foreign and security policy. ..However, minority rights of the Croatian community in Serbia, and especially the status of non-discriminatory use of the Croatian language, are still below European standards. This must change. Finally, we are still asking Serbia for the truth about missing persons from the Homeland War in order to move forward and to allow families to grieve with dignity.

Name: Thijs Reuten
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: we want Serbia to advance on its EU path. Instead, Serbia’s President Vučić is pulling his country away from the European Union, even if he says something else. Serbia’s leadership chooses regression on the rule of law over pro-European reforms. Its handling of this year’s elections demonstrates democracy is in clear peril...The EU is Serbia’s largest donor. Our support has long been steadfast. But we need to change tack; minimising Vučić’s clear autocratic tendencies and focusing on investment projects instead is a dead end. Accession negotiations with Serbia should only continue on two conditions: clear progress on the rule of law and full alignment with our sanctions on Russia.

Name: Peter van Dalen
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Serbia is doing exactly what the European Union is not doing. It supports Russia. Serbia has been under the spell of Russia for over a hundred years. That's why Serbia has not joined the EU sanctions against Russia. It also continues flights from Belgrade to Moscow and has purchased many weapons from Russia, Belarus, and China. Serbia disregards the European Union. The Serbian Orthodox Church blindly follows the Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church, Kirill. Moreover, the ties between the mafia in Serbia and Russia are already very close and intense. In short, let's remain unanimous. This country absolutely does not belong in the European Union.

Name: Alexander Alexandrov Yordanov
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Serbia's close cooperation with Russia, especially in the military sphere, poses a threat to European security...Recently, the Serbian Minister of Internal Affairs even spoke about the so-called "Serbian world" - a nationalist doctrine, copy-pasted from the "Russian world" doctrine, which has nothing to do with the values of European integration. Serbia needs to undertake a genuine process of disengagement from nationalist and Kremlin myths because the European Union does not need Russian Trojan horses.

Name: Tomislav Sokol
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: it is a fact that the accession negotiations for Serbia's entry into the EU are stagnating. There are many reasons for this situation. One of them is that Serbia is not a democratic country today; it is ruled by political unanimity, with complete domination by Vučić's progressives... Additionally, there is no visible desire or progress when it comes to the rule of law, fighting corruption, and implementing reforms. Throughout its history, Serbia has often shown a tendency for hegemony over neighboring countries... And, of course, they are acting in collusion and agreement with Russia. Before entering the EU, Serbia and its politicians must accept European values and address fundamental issues related to the rule of law, the state of democracy, the prosecution of war crimes, the cessation of aggressive interference in the politics of neighboring countries, and the clarification of the fate of missing persons from the aggression against Croatia.

Name: Joachim Stanisław Brudziński
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: After a very successful year 2021 for Serbia's accession process, its lack of response to Russia's aggression against Ukraine is disappointing. It has been argued here that Serbia is the only country in the region that has not joined any EU sanctions against Russia adopted after February 24. It is evident that Serbia, which is closer to Putin, Lavrov, the murderers from Bucha and Mariupol, Serbia that is closer to these atrocities committed by Russian soldiers against Ukrainian civilians, will not be able to join the European Union.

Name: Karlo Ressler
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: while the Ukrainian people are fighting for their own existence, for freedom, and for our European values, in Belgrade, Serbia, we are witnessing a sad and shameless calculation that is still ongoing, and we witness various ways of circumventing sanctions. In this way, Serbia is not only formally moving away from the European Union but also distancing itself from Europe in a civilizational sense. Secondly, what we are witnessing in our immediate neighborhood is unfortunately the elements of Serbia's old worn-out politics from the 1990s, where sincere and genuine cooperation is missing, especially in terms of reconciliation and addressing all remaining open issues from the 1990s...This is completely unacceptable, and as long as it continues, Serbia will not be ready for the European Union!

Name: Lukas Mandl
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Serbia is a beautiful country with great people, with a lot of cultural heritage. Serbia is a large country compared to the others in the Western Balkans and an economically strong country. It could serve a lot for the region and for all Europe. But I have to remind all of us about our decision in the plenary with a large majority on 1 March, about our deepest concern about Serbian behaviour when it comes to war on European soil...And it is also on Serbia to learn the lessons from history, to align with Europe and European values, to align with the sanctions which are the unbloody defence against the bloody war, and take the first in history, the status of our civilisation, for the sake of the Serbian people themselves.

Name: Sunčana Glavak
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Firstly, it's the suppression of media freedom in Serbia, which means that their citizens do not have a real insight into what is happening in their country. On the other hand, we do not have clear evidence and clear commitments, especially in terms of foreign policy, which is very important, where Serbia really wants to go. When it comes to the rule of law and democracy, I'm afraid that these are still unknown concepts for many Serbian politicians. Serbia must clearly demonstrate if it truly wants to follow the European path. This also means that it must address the issue of the missing from the Greater Serbian aggression on the Republic of Croatia, which is an obligation, I remind you, included in the accession negotiations.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: I agree, this Serbia has no place in the European Union. This is the same Serbia that provokes Kosovo. This is the same Serbia that provokes Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is the same Serbia that supports Russian propaganda during Russia's war against Ukraine. This is the same Serbia that hosts Russia's largest logistical intelligence center in the Balkans, in the whole of Europe, located in the city of Niš. I suppose you all know about that. This is the Serbia that oppresses national minorities...Yes, this Serbia suppresses Croats in its country, suppresses Bulgarians, violates their rights, oppresses them, seeks to resettle them, assimilate them, expel them, and continues to behave in an unacceptable and intolerable way. This is today's Serbia...This Serbia, which is a conduit for the Kremlin and Putin, has no place in the European Union, understand that.

Name: Janez Lenarčič
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: I also believe that the Russian aggression against Ukraine is a wake—up call on the need to accelerate the accession process for the Western Balkans. We have no time to lose...The Western Balkans remain a priority for the European Union...They called for the acceleration of this process – however, based on credible reforms by partners, fair and rigorous conditionality and the principles of own merits...Speaking about reforms, let me underline that the rule of law is a cornerstone of European values and it is a fundamental condition in the accession process. In 2020, the Commission adopted the revised enlargement methodology, which puts fundamental reforms – especially the rule of law – even further at the heart of the process and of our engagement.

Name: Kinga Gál
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Especially in these difficult times, it is of utmost importance to ensure stability and security in the Western Balkans. We should not slow down but accelerate the enlargement process in this region. Of course, each country must meet the accession criteria to maintain the credibility of the EU. The candidate status of the countries should be considered based on the same values and conditions. ...Hungary is one of the strongest supporters of the Western Balkans, including Serbia, in their EU accession process, and we firmly support Serbia's swift accession to the EU.

Name: Kinga Gál
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Especially in these difficult times, it is of utmost importance to ensure stability and security in the Western Balkans. We should not slow down but accelerate the enlargement process in this region. Of course, each country must meet the accession criteria to maintain the credibility of the EU. The candidate status of the countries should be considered based on the same values and conditions. Serbia has been waiting for progress in the accession process for years and is striving to meet the necessary EU requirements. However, the report does not contribute to Serbia's EU accession process; its excessive content may hinder it and alienate Serbia from the Union. ...Hungary is one of the strongest supporters of the Western Balkans, including Serbia, in their EU accession process, and we firmly support Serbia's swift accession to the EU.

Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: This year’s report only scratches the surface of the challenges and issues that are ahead for the Kosovo Government. Yet it also clearly underlines the long path Kosovo has made in the reforms and its euro integration. Kosovo keeps proving its democratic capacities by organis-ing free, fair and transparent elections. It is indeed a great example for all Western Balkan states of how to promote and nurture democratic standards, political dialogue and freedom of expression...Significant results have been achieved in the areas of the fight against corruption and organ-ised crime. The rule of law reforms need to be continued in line with the Venice Commission opinion and EU standards and for the benefit of all Kosovo’s citizens. These reforms, includ-ing the judiciary and anti-corruption agency reinforcement, are crucial for the European re-form agenda and Kosovo’s advancement on the EU accession path...An essential element on Kosovo’s EU integration path is certainly the dialogue between Ko-sovo and Serbia, which conditions the EU membership of both countries. Let me emphasise once again that without a comprehensive, legally binding agreement on the normalisation of relations between Kosovo and Serbia, accession to the Union will not occur...I have repeatedly reiterated the need for immediate granting of visa liberalisation, which is long overdue despite the fact that Kosovo has met all the criteria.

Name: Janez Lenarčič
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: It is worth noting that Kosovo has made a clear choice and reconfirmed its commitment to European values and to our Union. The government has condemned the Russian military aggression and demonstrated solidarity with Ukraine and with its people...We too need to keep our commitments. In July 2018, the Commission reported that Kosovo had fulfilled all the benchmarks to be granted visa liberalisation. The decision is still pending in the Council and we need to deliver on this long—overdue promise...Kosovo’s government continues to be resolute in its efforts to deliver EU—related reforms, including in key areas such as the fight against corruption and organised crime. We would like to see a faster pace of reform, including in the Assembly, which has a critical role to play in advancing the government’s EU agenda. We welcome Kosovo’s efforts to improve the efficiency, integrity and professionalism of the judiciary...More broadly, we expect Kosovo and Serbia to make rapid and concrete progress on the full normalisation of their relations. A comprehensive, legally—binding normalisation agree-ment is key for Serbia and Kosovo to advance on the European path. Let me end on this note: the entire region belongs in the European Union. They are part of the European family. Thank you for your attention.

Name: Janez Lenarčič
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Let me end on this note: the entire region belongs in the European Union. They are part of the European family. Thank you for your attention. // It is really important, perhaps more than ever before, that the European Union and this House express their full and unequivocal commitment to the EU membership perspective for all of the Western Balkans, including Kosovo.

Name: Lukas Mandl
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The entire Western Balkans – all six states – are crucial for the future of Europe.

Name: Lukas Mandl
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The entire Western Balkans – all six states – are crucial for the future of Europe...a state that has rapidly built democracy and the rule of law, a stable democracy with great diversity within the country. It is a rule of law that still requires reforms, but it has one of the most modern constitutions in the world as a backdrop.

Name: Andreas Schieder
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: In a summary, Kosovo is moving forward, is making progress. It’s more stable than it was before politically. And also it undertook a lot of reforms, but much more have to come also...The one is the Belgrade-Pristina dialogue, which has to be strengthened and emphasised, and the other one is the visa liberalisation. Every precondition is fulfilled, but still what we are missing is the green light for visa liberalisation.

Name: Ilhan Kyuchyuk
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Indeed, Kosovo is among the countries in the region where the EU integration process en-joys strong support among the citizens and all political actors. Without any doubt, Kosovo is arguably one of the most dedicated and loyal partner countries for the European Union. And again, it was a year that was dynamic and full of important political developments. But despite this, Kosovo has confirmed its strategic commitment to the European pact with the decision to formally apply to join the EU by the end of this year. Kosovo has proactively aligned with the EU’s common foreign and security policy and gave a great example by strongly condemning Russia’s aggression in Ukraine and became the first country from the region to join EU sanctions...It is so important, not for us as the European Union, but it’s important for our strategic rela-tionship with Kosovo

Name: Jean-Lin Lacapelle
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: the European Union is fanatically trying to convince itself that it remains an attractive force, seeking at all costs to integrate new countries within its ranks... It doesn't matter if it is a territory notorious for its mafia, Islamist activities, and trafficking, as illustrated by the present case of Kosovo. In fact, you want to open the doors of Europe to a massive influx of weapons, drug traffick-ing, human trafficking, and Islamist terrorism. I remind you that Kosovo has provided the highest number of jihadists to Syria and Iraq in Europe, proportionally to its population. Yet, you advocate for Kosovo's immediate accession to the European Union, as well as visa liber-alization for Kosovars, without caring that five EU Member States still do not recognize the existence of the territory.

Name: Andrey Kovatchev
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Kosovo has demonstrated commitment to implementing the necessary reforms, with strong public support for European integration. Now is the time for the government to utilize its stable majority in parliament and continue with the necessary reforms...I expect the government to take decisive actions to advance relations with Serbia, and here the clear goal, as we mentioned during the debate on Serbia, is mutual recognition of both sides.

Name: Thijs Reuten
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Kosovo played by the rules and fulfilled all the Commission benchmarks. Yet last month, the European Council failed them...Our leaders need to realize Europe’s geopolitical reality does not leave room for unending roadmaps. So I call on the Council and on the French and Dutch governments, in particular, to be resolute: end this irresponsible obstruction.

Name: Lars Patrick Berg
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)

Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)

When it comes, for example, to the approximation of the national legislation with the EU acquis, Georgia continues to be a frontrunner among the aspirants in the EU’s eastern neighbourhood. However, when it comes to demonstrating the ability of Georgia’s democratic structures and the country’s sustainable commitment to certain key European values, the narrow party political considerations and personal antagonisms of individual strongmen still seem to take priority over strategic national objectives...The 12 priorities identified by the Commission as a precondition for achieving EU candidate status should be seen as a helping hand, and Georgian authorities should seek to make the best use of it...As such, the statement points to a number of key problem areas in Georgia today – the independence of the judiciary, media freedom, as well as the need for an independent public defender...I believe that Georgia’s vital place is in Europe, but it’s for the Georgian politicians to deliver.

Name: Helena Dalli
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: The EU—Georgia Association Agreement remains a strong driver for reform, bringing the country closer to the EU’s values, principles, standards and legislation...So I start with the important reforms which have always been at the core of the EU—Georgia Association Agreement, and which are also reflected in the 12 priorities: an ambitious and comprehensive judicial reform, ensuring the independence, integrity and transparency of key judicial institutions, as well as systemic and inclusive review of the electoral legislation, remain essential. ..On the fight against corruption, a new anti-corruption bureau is due to be set up, and I want to underline the need to ensure that this bureau is truly independent...Turning now to the economic sectoral cooperation with Georgia, the process of aligning national law with EU law, as part of the Association Agreement, is overall on track and progressing in these areas. A thorough analysis of Georgia’s state of preparedness regarding the EU acquis is due by the end of this year...This is a crucial moment for the whole country to unite and work resolutely for the common strategic goal of EU membership. // With regard to a timeline for Georgia to join the EU, as you know becoming a member of the European Union is not something that happens overnight. It is subject to a thorough process involving substantial work across all membership criteria. So the pace of accession depends on the progress in reform, first and foremost in the fundamental areas, starting with the rule of law.

Name: Markéta Gregorová
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: We have been pointing out for years that the areas of democracy, rule of law, fundamental freedoms and human rights in Georgia have significant issues without improvement on many elements, which is why the report on Georgia is somewhat critical.

Name: Miriam Lexmann
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: We must acknowledge that the progress in some sectoral reforms has taken place, but we cannot ignore the overall state of democratic processes and rule of law...Overcoming these serious challenges is the key to Georgia’s European future, but also in strengthening the country’s democracy, as well as the resilience in light of today’s Georgian situation. As friends of the Georgian people and the champions of their European aspirations, we must be honest about these developments and not waiver in our support for Georgia’s democracy.

Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: The government has borrowed a page or two from Putin’s disinformation handbook. It is spreading lies against the EU, the US, and even against NATO. It is nothing but a shameless lie that the West wants to drag Georgia into the war. Media freedom is deteriorating while pro-Russian radicals are allowed to unleash violence on the media and minority.... Ten years ago, he promised an amazing democracy but delivered a captured state. Because of all this, Georgia did not get the candidate status. The EU integration is in Georgia’s constitution. And those who fail will have to answer to future generations.

Name: Bernhard Zimniok
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: Bringing Georgia closer to the EU is another attempt to expand the external borders all the way to Asia, while the problems in Europe are far from being solved. This new enlargement project will only further strain our resources. There isn't even a land connection to Georgia, but its accession would shift the EU's borders towards Russia, Turkey, and Azerbaijan. Not only does this pose significant conflict potential with such neighbors, but it also opens the door to new migration flows. ...Each new member state will make protecting the Schengen borders even more difficult – terrible news for the majority of European citizens.

Name: Adam Bielan
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: in view of the Kremlin’s illegal war waged against Ukraine, the European Parliament’s involvement in and support to Georgia has become even more crucial to the stability of the region. Georgia is one of the founding members of the Eastern Partnership and remains a key partner of the European Union. However, I would like to highlight a few short- and long—term objectives of our work together, which still remain to be achieved...Second, Russian propaganda and disinformation campaigns are swiftly spreading in Georgia and are objects of political utilisation. These two issues are not acceptable for a candidate country, especially in the current context, and should be addressed immediately. If they are not resolved, Georgia should not be granted candidate status.

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Georgia belongs in Europe. It was torn away from Europe by force by Soviet Russia. Today, 20% of its territory is still under Russian occupation. The remaining bloodstained dividing lines in Europe imposed by Stalin and Hitler must be erased. Georgia’s membership of the EU is the best way to achieve it. I am convinced that Georgia will be a member of the European Union. The Georgian people deserve it. I am also sure that EU enlargement makes the EU stronger, including its security...The Georgian authorities know very well what they have to do. All is written in the recommendation of the Commission and they have to do it without manipulations or pretence. Keeping the seriously—ill former President Mikhail Saakashvili in prison is not a European value. Torturing people is Putin’s policy.

Name: Juozas Olekas
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: It has indeed been said that Georgia is an important partner for us, and the Georgian people have repeatedly expressed their choice for a European path. However, as the Commissioner mentioned, the bar has been set high for Georgia, and we are waiting for Georgia to implement the 12 recommendations that were presented. We can note that Georgia is making some progress, especially in the fight against corruption and in the field of digital security. However, it is important to emphasize that the rule of law, the implementation of democracy, and the rights of a free press are still not at the level we would like them to be

Name: Joachim Stanisław Brudziński
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Poland and Georgia are countries that have a centuries-old, very close cooperation – that is why Georgia is Poland's priority partner in the South Caucasus region. ..We also reaffirm our unwavering support for Georgia's Euro-Atlantic aspirations. Poland upholds its commitment to the open-door policy regarding Georgia's future full membership in the European Union and NATO. There is no alternative, especially since the Georgian people strongly support this direction. However, it must be said clearly: Georgia will never join the European Union if it treats politicians in such inhumane and bestial ways

Name: David McAllister
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Georgia is part of Europe. Georgia belongs to Europe. But as we have heard tonight, to be granted EU candidate status, Georgia needs to successfully address the 12 key priorities indicated by the Commission. The Georgian bid for membership will continue to be assessed based on its own merits and its success in implementing all the necessary reforms...First, political stakeholders need to refrain from any divisive and aggressive rhetoric, and unite their forces in order to increase trust among all political and institutional actors. Second, the excessive influence of vested interests in economic, political and public life needs to be eliminated. Third, Georgian authorities need to ensure media freedom. This entails editorial independence, transparent media ownership of pluralistic, impartial and non-discriminatory coverage of political views. Fourth, political leaders in Georgia must stop aggressive verbal attacks against Members of our European Parliament and representatives of other partner countries.

Name: Cristian Terheş
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: The Georgian nation and people need our support and a strong sign from the EU now. Georgia’s place is in the EU, and they need our unequivocal support to achieve this goal.

Name: Lukas Mandl
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Georgia has a clear tendency towards the European Union, European values. A lot has to be done in terms of reforms when it comes to the rule of law, when it comes to fighting corruption, when it comes to also proper political competition, not political fight on a sometimes basis of hatred in the country, when it comes to media freedom. But one could feel and can feel in Georgia that there is a clear European attitude in the population, and as the other parts of the Eastern Partnership, meaning here Ukraine and the Republic of Moldova, Georgia can become an EU Member State in the future undergoing these reforms

Name: Liudas Mažylis
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Since 2016, Georgia has made considerable efforts to implement economic, human rights, and anti-corruption reforms envisaged in the Association Agreement and has been a leading country in the Eastern Partnership. With the outbreak of Russia's aggressive war in Ukraine, on March 3rd, Georgia submitted an application for EU membership. However, all it received was a recognition of the European perspective this June. This positive news is too little for Georgia.

Name: Seán Kelly
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Obviously, because of the war in Ukraine, things have changed dramatically, and more and more countries in an eastern neighbourhood see not just their economic viability, but their actual viability per se, as being guaranteed only by joining the European Union and that is something which we should be proud of, but something we should facilitate. And I think in relation to countries like Georgia, they should be given a time-limit by which they reach the standards required. Having countries like Georgia and Moldova and others on a list ad infinitum, stretching them out, is not fair to them. So, there should be a time limit by which they’re told: you reach these targets by then, otherwise, you wait for another ten years. But you need some type of certainty, and I think that’s what Georgia needs now, because they would be very valuable Members of the European Union.

Name: Seán Kelly
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Obviously, because of the war in Ukraine, things have changed dramatically, and more and more countries in an eastern neighbourhood see not just their economic viability, but their actual viability per se, as being guaranteed only by joining the European Union and that is something which we should be proud of, but something we should facilitate. But you need some type of certainty, and I think that’s what Georgia needs now, because they would be very valuable Members of the European Union.

Name: Urmas Paet
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Before obtaining candidate country status, Georgia must address a list of crucial tasks. Taking the necessary steps before the next evaluation by the European Commission should be the overarching goal of all political forces in Georgia. This is a historic opportunity for Georgia that must be seized. Political determination is needed to support the clear backing of the Georgian people for their country's integration into the EU. Additionally, political polarization must be overcome, as it only harms the country

Name: Pål Jonson
Type: Member of Council of the EU
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Tomorrow the EU leaders will reiterate our support and encouragement to Ukraine’s reform efforts, which are particularly impressive considering these difficult times, and we will commit to further deepening our relationship, including through the new priority action plan for the DCFTA 2023-2024, easing Ukraine’s access to our internal market.

Name: Johannes Hahn
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: We will discuss the reform efforts by Ukraine, the further alignment of its legislation with the EU acquis, and we will outline further steps to enhance sectoral cooperation. Ukraine’s destiny is in Europe. Our common European path was decided last June by granting the status of candidate country to Ukraine. The Commission will support Ukraine throughout the whole accession process, despite the continuing ruthless attacks of the aggressor we are seeing a major momentum of reforms in Ukraine.... The discussions in Kiev today and tomorrow will focus on reform priorities and the steps necessary to help Ukraine further align its legislation to the Union acquis, following the Commission’s analytical report which was just published complementing the Commission’s opinion on Ukraine’s EU membership application...Russia’s military aggression has shown that Ukraine belongs to Europe. We share the same values, the same aspiration for democracy and freedom, and we will stay united for as long as it takes.

Name: Iratxe García Pérez
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The European Union-Ukraine summit must also convey a clear message to the Ukrainian authorities on their path towards the European Union: Ukraine needs a rule of law with strong institutions that protect citizens and guarantee their rights. The end of the road will come when Ukraine receives and contributes to the European Union what the European Union receives and contributes to each Member State: democracy, economic growth, and social cohesion...With confidence in our Union, there are reasons to continue looking to the future with hope. It is the responsibility of the Ukrainian people and the rest of European societies aspiring to live in a free world to continue deciding our destiny together.

Name: Stéphane Séjourné
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Ukrainians bear the security of the European Union on their shoulders. Yet, Ukrainians are not yet members of our Union, and thus, they do not participate in our decisions. That's why our Parliament has always been the voice, right here, of the Ukrainian people in this war...The gradual integration of Ukraine into our bloc is also an absolute priority: the common market, structural programs, and European funds must be progressively opened to our Ukrainian friends. At every stage of sanctions and integration, we know that the Kremlin will threaten us.

Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: But winning the war alone will not be enough for an EU membership. Other fundamental steps need to be taken, the sooner the better. Even during a war, Ukraine is fighting corruption. This progress should now be made structural and accelerated tenfold. Societies in Europe need assurance that oligarchs pulling dirty schemes, governmental officials stealing from the army, and judges robbing the country will all be brought to justice fairly and transparently. Media freedom cannot be compromised, not even during wartime. Democracy is strong when power is shared, not monopolised. This is what sets apart Ukraine from Russia. Ukraine is a European state with a European future. Its people will not walk the European path alone. They have the entire democratic world behind them.

Name: Beata Szydło
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: The future of Ukraine lies in the European Union. Ukraine is determined to end the war as quickly as possible, to win the war, and to become a member of the European Union. The European Union needs Ukraine, just as Ukraine needs the European Union...I want to say that I am proud of Poland, which shows every day that it understands that the future of the European Union, the security of the European Union, and the security of all of us depend on Ukraine's victory.

Name: Tamás Deutsch
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: We stand on the side of the attacked and support Ukraine's independence and territorial integrity. We also support Ukraine's European Union membership.

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Ukraine must be invited to EU membership negotiations – not some day, but this year. Our goal is to grant EU membership to Ukraine before the end of this decade. Bold and swift EU decisions on Ukraine’s future in EU will help the country to ultimately defeat Putin...The EU must act as a geopolitical leader because this is a historic chance for us all. We need Ukraine.

Name: Petras Auštrevičius
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: as a project for peace and cooperation, the European Union has withstood many historical challenges, and remains highly appreciated and enjoyed by its citizens. Ukraine’s aspiration to join our Union is an understandable logical and right choice. For Ukraine, European Union membership means choosing between democracy and Russian authoritarianism, between freedom and occupation. The granting of candidate status to Ukraine has justified the EU’s nature as an open and forward-looking geopolitical actor. Our trusted partner – which continues democratic reforms while resisting Russia’s war of aggression – needs to be invited to start accession negotiations now. Such a decision will not only testify to our commitment to our neighbourhood policy, but will also strengthen Ukraine as a state, raise the spirits of Ukrainians and give them hope.

Name: Sergey Lagodinsky
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Now we must make our EU fit for the important challenge of enlargement and make Ukraine - its society and economy - fit for the Union. It will be a long road, and our Ukrainian friends know this, but we are walking this road together. And that is our logic of peace, that is our logic of peace.

Name: Anna Fotyga
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: And Commissioner, running marathon in times of earthquake and people shedding their blood for our values is not advisable. We have to have clear timeline agreed with Ukraine for accession to the EU and NATO.

Name: Mick Wallace
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: Zelenskyy has now banned 12 opposition parties and used the war to carry through deeply anti-democratic labour reforms. The International Trade Union Confederation, which unites more than 200 million workers worldwide, are protesting against the laws...Since when did handing over public assets to big business ever help the people of any country? This is a programme for even deeper corruption and inequality. The EU is promising the sun, moon and stars to Ukraine, including fast—tracking EU accession. Be careful what you wish for!

Name: Włodzimierz Cimoszewicz
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Ukraine cannot afford to lose because it would destroy the European order based on respect for the law...We want Ukraine to join us within the framework of the European Union, and we are ready to open the path for the rapid start of accession negotiations. This will be crucial to maintain optimism and belief in Ukraine's bright future. However, everyone must understand that EU enlargement is not only a political process, and we cannot make unrealistic promises. This could lead to disappointment.

Name: Guy Verhofstadt
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: And finally, a fast—track membership to 2026. If I see what is happening on corruption in Hungary, I think, and I see the actions that are happening in Ukraine, Ukraine deserves a place in Europe.

Name: Markéta Gregorová
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: I am an unapologetic fan of EU enlargement, which is why I welcome Presidents Zelinskyy’s commitment to reforms – changing legal, social and political reality to align with our European acquis, even during wartime. I have high hopes for the upcoming summit to bring Ukraine even closer to the EU family. In the European family, they already are.

Name: Witold Jan Waszczykowski
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Secondly, what I expect from the summit is a clear and fast perspective of membership of the European Union based on the Copenhagen criteria and the acquis communautaire and nothing else. We cannot treat Ukraine as a guinea pig, as a laboratory of liberal visions.

Name: Siegfried Mureşan
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: we have all seen this year that we can only live in safety and stability within the borders of the European Union if we are surrounded in our Eastern Neighbourhood by countries which are safe, stable, at peace. This is why I am telling to you today that the fight that the people of Ukraine are fighting is also our fight. This is why it is right to support Ukraine and it is also in the fundamental interest of the European Union to support Ukraine...make sure that even before EU accession becomes possible, we bring Ukraine closer to European projects. Integration into the single market will help Ukraine, will help ourselves and the principle: whatever we do for Ukraine we do for Moldova as well.

Name: Siegfried Mureşan
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: we have all seen this year that we can only live in safety and stability within the borders of the European Union if we are surrounded in our Eastern Neighbourhood by countries which are safe, stable, at peace. This is why I am telling to you today that the fight that the people of Ukraine are fighting is also our fight. Integration into the single market will help Ukraine, will help ourselves and the principle: whatever we do for Ukraine we do for Moldova as well.

Name: Tonino Picula
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The key message of the summit must be that we stand with Ukraine and count on its European Union perspective.

Name: Dragoş Tudorache
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: I hear more and more arguing that giving hope to Ukraine and Moldova last year when accepting their candidate status was wrong because it created false expectations. Well yes, that historic decision did create expectations, legitimate expectations that once we went down the path of thinking and acting strategically, geopolitically, that we would stay on that path. Working hard to start the process of accession negotiations, like our resolution says, is the minimum that we must do to be consistent with ourselves and with the commitment that we made to the Ukrainian cause and people.

Name: Dragoş Tudorache
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: I hear more and more arguing that giving hope to Ukraine and Moldova last year when accepting their candidate status was wrong because it created false expectations. Well yes, that historic decision did create expectations, legitimate expectations that once we went down the path of thinking and acting strategically, geopolitically, that we would stay on that path. Working hard to start the process of accession negotiations, like our resolution says, is the minimum that we must do to be consistent with ourselves and with the commitment that we made to the Ukrainian cause and people.

Name: Jakop G. Dalunde
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Ukraine belongs to Europe...It is no coincidence that there is a different democratic aspiration in the Ukraine we see today - which differs from Russian society - and that is what Putin is afraid of. That is why historical falsification is taking place, because Putin does not want to acknowledge that Ukraine is something different and that Ukraine belongs in Europe.

Name: Ryszard Czarnecki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: I want to say very clearly that this is a very important summit. We need to support Ukraine's accession to the European Union and NATO.

Name: Andrius Kubilius
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: From another side, the EU needs to assist Russians with the inspirational example of the success of Ukraine. Such a success of Ukraine can be created only through Ukraine’s integration into EU, just like the success story of the Central Europe was created. Ukraine’s geopolitical integration into the West is no less important than Leopards or Abrams for Ukraine’s defence because this is the only way to sustainable peace on the European continent. And that is why the summit should establish the ‘Integration Ramstein’ in order also to deliver integration

Name: Nathalie Loiseau
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: I also hear that Ukraine is eager to join the European Union and that its enthusiasm should be curbed. But come on, in the midst of war, Ukraine is continuing its reforms. In the midst of war, President Zelensky is fighting corruption on an unprecedented scale, and let's say it, without an equivalent in some of our member states.

Name: Márton Gyöngyösi
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: the people of Ukraine expressed unequivocally their desire to join the community of Western democracies instead of Moscow’s tyranny. Europe was right to hear that desire and grant candidate status to Ukraine. However, full membership has conditions that need to be fulfilled. Sustainable peace and stability need to be attained prior to integration in order to avoid taking on a divided country with internal division...Second, Ukraine needs to reach out to ethnic minorities living in its territory – all of them – and guarantee their rights as Ukrainian citizens and ethnic minorities.

Name: Vilija Blinkevičiūtė
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The unjustified military aggression by Russia has irrevocably changed the geopolitical situation in all of Europe. And the whole world has seen the true face of Russia and the Kremlin regime. Therefore, now is the time to focus and make decisive political, economic, and financial decisions to help Ukraine fight and defeat Russia's aggression. Let us not forget that Ukraine's victory against Russia is the guarantee of all our security, freedom, and democracy. Therefore, an agreement must be reached on...  of course, the uninterrupted, particularly military, and all-round assistance to Ukraine, as well as a firm commitment to support Ukraine's membership in the European Union.

Name: Traian Băsescu
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Regarding Ukraine's European aspirations, in this regard, Ukraine must understand that the new minority law must be brought into the form recommended by the Venice Commission to guarantee the rights of minorities.

Name: Herbert Dorfmann
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: But then, in the coming months and years, we must ensure that, in a process of approximation to the European Union, the standards of the European Union are also adhered to in Ukraine.

Name: Riho Terras
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Ukraine has fought bravely against Russia for almost nine years. The full—scale attack that Russia launched in February last year is a clear sign that Putin’s regime goal is to destroy Western way of life. Our task is to help Ukraine as much as they need today. Ukraine needs more weapons and Ukraine needs a plan for recovery. The EU—Ukraine summit must give Ukraine a message of hope. Ukraine belongs to European family.

Name: Ivan Štefanec
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The future of Europe is being decided in Ukraine. It is about whether we will protect life, defend the rights of the weaker, and democratically decide about our future or, God forbid, the other side wins – disrespect for life, lawlessness, and the will of a dictator. Ukrainians are defending our space, defending freedom and democracy across Europe, and it is our moral duty to help them..We talk about the European peace project, but no one has done as much for peace in Europe as the Ukrainians. Therefore, it is important to help them on their European path and concretize this path at the upcoming summit, which starts tomorrow.

Name: Juozas Olekas
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: you are very right when you said that the future of Ukraine is in Europe. But today, the future of Europe is being decided in Ukraine, and therefore we can achieve peace only if Putin's aggressors leave Ukrainian soil and Ukraine's territorial integrity is restored. For that to happen, at the meeting we are talking about, it must be ensured that ...the European Union starts negotiations for Ukraine's accession to the European Union this year. I also want to emphasize that it is crucial to connect Ukraine with the European Union

Name: Georgios Kyrtsos
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: After all, we are dealing with a European war. We all know that if the Russians are not stopped and defeated in Ukraine, they will continue towards Moldova, the Baltic states, maybe Poland. During the past 20 years, we have been encouraging Ukraine’s European ambitions without offering adequate support. Our goal should be the integration of Ukraine in the European Union based on an unprecedented programme of economic support.

Name: Maria Grapini
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: But Ukraine must understand, as a state that has signed an accession agreement, that it must respect the rights of minorities, and that is why I ask you, Mr. Commissioner, to verify the respect for the status, the agreement that Ukraine has signed, because yes, Romanian minorities cannot speak Romanian, cannot learn in Romanian, and now there have been oppressions against Romanian Orthodox priests.

Name: Andrea Bocskor
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Russia's unjust war against Ukraine, which I completely condemn, presents the country and its population with unprecedented challenges, but it must continue its reforms to progress on the path of EU accession. In the shadow of war, implementing reforms requires great effort from Ukraine, but meeting the criteria for EU membership, including the Copenhagen criteria and the conditions set by the European Commission in June, is an essential requirement for accession! One of these conditions is guaranteeing the rights of national minorities. However, in December, the Ukrainian parliament adopted a new law on national minorities that was not consulted with the Venice Commission and did not take into account the views of representatives of national minorities when the text was adopted. As a result, the law does not guarantee the enforcement and protection of the fundamental rights of national minorities, and it does not improve, for example, the situation of the Hungarian minority living in Ukraine, but merely solidifies the restrictions caused by the 2017 Education Law and the 2019 Language Law

Name: Kinga Gál
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Our position is clear: we support Ukraine's EU accession and fully condemn Russia's aggression against Ukraine. We also support the reconstruction of the country, but for this, the establishment of peace is needed instead of a sanctions policy that deepens the economic difficulties of the Member States. This is primarily in the interest of the population of Ukraine. In the accession process, the same conditions must apply as for the other candidate countries. Thus, compliance with the Copenhagen criteria is also crucial, as the enforcement of the rights of Hungarian, Romanian, and Bulgarian minorities living in Ukraine is one of the prerequisites for accession negotiations. Indeed, these minority communities could be the most committed supporters of Ukraine's European perspective.

Name: Marian-Jean Marinescu
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: There is no doubt that Ukraine's place is in the EU. However, for a smooth integration, the accession process must be well planned. Ahead of the EU-Ukraine summit in Kyiv, we adopted a resolution in the Parliament expressing the European legislature's vision on consolidating Ukraine's European path. Thus, the Kyiv summit should give priority to establishing an EU package of measures for Ukraine's recovery and starting accession negotiations, as well as agreeing on the need for a roadmap for Ukraine's accession to the EU's single market. Additionally, the Ukrainian authorities are invited to respond to the pro-European choice of the citizens and accelerate the process of adopting the necessary reforms to efficiently meet the criteria for EU accession.

Name: Josep Borrell Fontelles
Type: Member of Council of the EU
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: But Ukrainians look to Europe as many other peoples - including mine - looked at it, as a promising future. Their journey may be long because the war will be long, but we must make every effort to ensure that this promise is not frustrated; so that, on the contrary, Ukraine emerges victorious from this war and finds in the European family, to which it al-ready de facto belongs, the future it needs. // I have never seen any country that had such an existential hope in the idea of Europe as Ukraine has. Europe has always been, for peoples who lived in dictatorships deprived of freedom—like mine—a lighthouse in the night guiding our will and future. But I have never seen a country for which belonging to the European Union was so existential as it is for Ukraine.

Name: Ursula von der Leyen
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: During our visit to Kyiv, we agreed on a roadmap to further improve Ukraine's access to our single market. Putin wanted to kill Ukraine's European dream, but today, Ukraine is moving towards the European Union faster and more resolutely than ever...And that brings us to our third task ahead. We want to build a bridge of hope for the Ukrain-ian people - from the horrors of the war they are living in today to a better future among us. Rebuilding Ukraine, and its progress on the path towards our Union go hand in hand. You’ve heard it from President Zelenskyy in this very hemicycle, I’ve seen it with my College in Kyiv, I know it from the colleagues at the Commission who confirm it every single day: Ukrainians are making tangible progress despite the war, despite fighting the aggressor. They know that the accession to our Union is a merit-based process. They have passed legis-lative reforms that others thought would take years. They are making this progress because they are striving for Europe with all their heart and soul. Ukraine is a nation defined not only by its history and heritage, it is a nation defined by its dreams, and Europe is one of these dreams. So, distinguished Members, let’s honour these dreams by standing up for Ukraine for as long as it takes, so that one day the representatives of the Ukrainian people will have their place in this very hemicycle. Long live europe, slava Ukraini!

Name: Manfred Weber
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)

The EU is and will remain Serbia’s main po-litical and economic partner, investor and donor and continues to support the country on its EU path. // So we count on Serbia as a sincere European partner to stand with us and for our common values and for our common interests, our security and prosperity. Name: Željana Zovko
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Serbia is making progress on its European path, but it still needs to address significant chal-lenges. Normalizing relations with Kosovo and resolving all ongoing bilateral issues with neighboring countries are also important factors for Serbia's progress.

Name: Dimitris Papadakis
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: I recognize that difficulties persist, and there is still much work to be done. However, I also acknowledge that some progress has been made.
