I conclude with the following message: we fully support Serbia's European perspective and advocate for a peaceful future for all the country's inhabitants within the European family.

Name: Klemen Grošelj
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The report, the last in this term, paints a rather bleak picture of Serbia as a candidate coun-try. Progress is limited or simply absent. The gap between commitments made and their implementation continues to widen. There are too many examples of this. Perhaps the most striking one is the case of the removal of prosecutors who were investigating corruption in Elektroprivreda Srbije. This case clearly shows that the independence of the judiciary re-mains an unfulfilled goal despite constitutional and legal changes. Similarly bleak is the state of the media, where the dominant position of the state-owned Telekom is strengthening, and its business practices from the perspective of competition protection are, to say the least, unusual...But these are symptoms. The root cause lies in the fact that the current Serbian leadership is content with such a state of affairs. The Serbian authorities do not have a genuine desire to move closer to the EU and enter it to improve the well-being of their citizens. For them, the EU is just one of the stages of domestic and foreign policy battles.

Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: despite many efforts, Serbia is not much more democratic than it has been before. It’s a country that still lacks genuine democratic standards and fair elections, as well as freedom of expression and political culture. I would like to remind Mr Vučić and the Serbian government to deliver on two things: one, the domestic reforms. Nothing else can replace our request for reaching the highest Europe-an standards, rule of law, media freedom, free market competition and the fight against corruption. This is the key, not because Europe asks for that, but because the lives of Serbian citizens will improve. Two, the dialogue with Kosovo. It needs to be centred on the people, from finding all missing persons to ensuring that Kosovo Serbs are not the puppets in anyone’s hands. Serbia needs to close the Kosovo chapter and move on from the past. These two points are crucial for Serbia to become a true EU candidate that can join the Un-ion. There are indeed progressive forces in Serbia fighting firmly for our common values.

Name: Joachim Stanisław Brudziński
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: However, when it comes to Serbia, the strategic directions of Belgrade's foreign policy unfor-tunately remain unchanged, while the Russian aggression against Ukraine clearly showed that Serbia is finding it increasingly difficult to maintain a multi-vector policy. Balancing be-tween East and West, hiding behind the protection of its own economic interests, and pro-Russian sentiments, the Serbian authorities have not yet decided to join sanctions against Russia. Over the past months, there has been a noticeable decline in the alignment of Ser-bia's foreign policy with the EU's common foreign and security policy...Lack of alignment between Serbia and the European Union was also evident in relation to China, Iran, Belarus, and others. Given the growing lack of alignment of Serbian foreign poli-cy with the EU's policy, the chances of making progress in the accession negotiation pro-cess, including the opening of another negotiating cluster in the first half of 2023, are slim, or practically non-existent...It must be said that Serbia with Putin will obviously not join the European Union.

Name: Thierry Mariani
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: the European Union is not a friend of the Serbian people. The list of its demands towards Belgrade is endless, while Brussels constantly supports the demands of Kosovo. The EU in-stitutions supported the amputation of Serbia's historical cradle, Kosovo...At the same time, the European Union is pressuring Serbia to transform its political and social life. Brussels would like to sever Belgrade's historical friendship with Russia, including dictating its foreign policy from now on. We have no interest in building a European perspective in the Balkans if it is based on the Atlanticism that Brussels wants to impose on Serbia

Name: Emmanuel Maurel
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: Like us, the Serbian people aspire to peace and democracy, and I believe this is the meaning of the sincere and positive dialogue that the European Union must have with a country that has been a candidate for accession since 2012 and has made undeniable progress in at least half of the negotiation chapters. But is it enough? Obviously not. Serbia needs to act to ex-pand its media space, to have more trust in civil society, and, of course, to continue its poli-cy of reconciliation towards Bosnia. It also needs to find a lasting solution with Kosovo...Under the pretext that Serbia is not fully aligned with our foreign policy, it should be treated harshly. I disagree with that. I think it would make no sense to open up to the Balkans with-out taking Serbia into account. I believe that such an attitude actually leads to the opposite of the desired goal, as it does not serve the interests of Serbia or the European Union. Let us be consistent and continue to reach out to Serbia, which has much to expect from us.

Name: Kinga Gál
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Serbia is the region's main stabilizing force and a key country, so its early accession to Eu-rope is in the interest of all. The country has been waiting for progress in the accession pro-cess for years and is striving to meet the EU's conditions. ..We need to accelerate the accession negotiations rather than intensify geopolitical tensions. Especially now, when the stability of the region has become even more valuable due to the Russian-Ukrainian war, the energy crisis, and migration pressures.

Name: Tonino Picula
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: These tragic events are a reminder of Serbia's chronic problems - personal rule by one man, the occupation of the state and its institutions, glorification of war criminals, and a toxic media scene. Key democratic indicators confirm that Serbia is stagnating on its European path. Continued financial support to the Aleksandar Vučić regime through investment projects does not bring Serbia closer to the European Union, nor does it distance it from Putin's Rus-sia...But there is full support for the citizens who clearly want a different, better, and European Serbia, a Serbia without violence. They prove that there is capacity for change. Without them, there will be a continuing crisis with negative impacts on the whole region, and the EPP, of which Vučić's party is a part, has a special responsibility for communicating Europe-an values to the official Belgrade.

Name: Valter Flego
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: I call on the Serbian authorities, if they really want changes, to turn to building a new Ser-bia...For years now, we have been repeating what the Union asks of Serbia - strengthening insti-tutions, fighting corruption, and ensuring independent media. However, the real question today is what Serbia wants from the Union and whether it even wants the Union and all its fundamental values...talk about the future, one that the people will define, about concrete demands and ques-tions that will pave the way for the creation of a new Serbia, a European Serbia. And that new Serbia, woven on the wings of democracy and the rule of law, if it so desires, will undoubtedly have its place in a united Europe.

Name: Ladislav Ilčić
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Serbia is not committed to European values and never has been. You wonder why it hasn't imposed sanctions on Russia. You are curious about why it toler-ates volunteers joining the criminal Wagner paramilitary unit. You are puzzled as to how Russian propaganda media can freely broadcast on Serbian territory. Let me tell you how it is possible. Everything Russia is doing today, Serbia has been doing for over a hundred years, not only with weapons as it did 30 years ago, but also by stealing culture and the Croatian language...You can give billions to Serbia, but it will still look towards Moscow because that relation-ship is part of their history, identity, and political mindset. Allowing such Serbia to enter the European Union would mean having a full member of a small Russia undermining this community from within in the interest of the big Russia.

Name: Miriam Lexmann
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: In particular, I would like to highlight the strong emphasis on countering the malign influ-ence and hybrid threats from non—democratic regimes, particularly including the Chinese Communist Party. Chinese corrosive capital continues to cause environmental damages, undermines good governance, and even the EU acquis passed down through the enlargement process. The growing influence of these regimes continues to negatively impact the future develop-ment of Serbia and its neighbours. It is absolutely crucial for the European Union to combine a sustainable alternative to Chinese investment with the necessary political commitment to Serbia’s – and the region’s – democracy and EU membership.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: The same foreign policy of denying national states, following the Comintern line, creating fake nations, denying the real nations, suppressing these nations within Serbia, suppressing national minorities. ..But this Serbia has never been European and will never be European...This Serbia that you support actually mocks all of you behind your backs; it pursues policies of genocide, policies of denying national minorities, and it's essentially pursuing an anti-European policy.

Name: Eugen Tomac
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Returning to political issues, it is extremely important to look at the truth as it is and to tell those in Belgrade that they must stop their double talk regarding Serbia's European path. Name: Tomislav Sokol
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)

Name: Sunčana Glavak
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: However, the key problems we identified still remain, and I would like to ask if the authori-ties in Serbia are really listening to us, Commissioner. Especially when it comes to sanctions towards Russia and relations with Kosovo, high levels of corruption, human rights issues, not to mention the state of media freedom, organized crime, and the prosecution of war crimes. Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)

Name: Olivér Várhelyi
Party: Other - Not specified

Name: Lukas Mandl

Name: Andreas Schieder
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)

Be-cause we need a stable Balkans, and Kosovo belongs in Europe as well.

Name: Ilhan Kyuchyuk
Party: Renew Europe (RE)

Name: Romeo Franz
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Kosovo belongs in the EU...An obstacle to Kosovo's future development is Serbia's blocking stance, which prevents mu-tual normalization of relations.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: there is hardly a more pro-Western and pro-European community in Europe than in Kosovo. And yes, the people in Kosovo deserve support for their efforts. And the people in Kosovo deserve the negotiation process to start faster and to be part of the European Union...The Republic of Kosovo and Kosovars deserve to be part of this Union.

Name: Jean-Lin Lacapelle
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: the forced integration of Kosovo into the European Union is a disaster that has already cost European taxpayers 1.2 billion euros over the past fifteen years. Name: Fabio Massimo Castaldo
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)

Name: Fabio Massimo Castaldo
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)

Equally important at this moment is to continue the dialogue with Belgrade to increase mu-tual trust, overcome inter-ethnic divisions, and normalize the relations between the two countries.

Name: Thijs Reuten
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: But let this report and visa-free travel be the prelude to a new chapter: Kosovo's EU inte-gration path. The inclusion of all countries in the region into the European family - including Kosovo - contributes to stability and a good future for everyone there, but it is also in the interest of the EU as a whole and our shared continent.

Name: Ryszard Czarnecki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Let's talk about Kosovo. I want to say clearly: there are certain issues that need to be re-solved in this country, such as corruption and the resolution of bilateral issues between Ko-sovo and Serbia. These are serious challenges for our partner. Let's not pretend that these challenges do not exist. We must set conditions and demand certain changes, especially in the country's legislation regarding the fight against corruption.

Name: Carles Puigdemont i Casamajó
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: the future of Kosovo is international recognition and Europe. The efforts being made by Ko-sovo society and institutions deserve more of both: more international recognition and more Europe...Unfortunately, there are still EU countries that do not recognise Kosovo. Some of them, like Spain, for reasons that have nothing to do with Kosovo, but with Catalonia.

Name: Sunčana Glavak
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: To begin with, the normalization of relations between Kosovo and Serbia is necessary, which means mutual recognition, and it is crucial for securing the European future of both coun-tries. I welcome Kosovo's application for membership in the European Union, as the Commission-er also mentioned, but what is essential is the constant pro-European orientation of its citi-zens and a majority cross-party consensus on integration into the European Union, as well as a clear geostrategic political choice. Kosovo has demonstrated its dedication to European integration by implementing reforms in key areas. When I mention this, it is about the rule of law, human freedom, and progress in media freedom. However, despite progress, Kosovo faces numerous challenges, the need for further strengthening of institutions, reforms, and improvement of the social and economic situa-tion in Kosovo.

Name: Clare Daly
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: anyone reading this report would think that nearly all of Kosovo’s problems have magically vanished. Grand, but let’s not pretend that it is anything to do with the real world.

Party: Renew Europe (RE)

Name: Paulo Rangel

Name: Olivér Várhelyi
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: We believe in Bosnia Herzegovina and therefore the Commission recommended to grant candidate status to the country, which was followed by a decision of the European Council last December. This is the agenda with real gains and real benefits for everyone. It is the agenda that brings prosperity, stability and peace. And it is the agenda on which we need to work on together. We, at the Commission, are ready to support Bosnia and Herzegovina in this work and with all our instruments.

Name: Željana Zovko

Name: Dietmar Köster
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: the annual report underscores BiH’s momentum on its path to the European Union now that it has been granted candidate status. But there is still much to be done. Name: Klemen Grošelj
Party: Renew Europe (RE)

Name: Tineke Strik
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Chair, we awarded the candidate status to Bosnia in December last year. Now, both sides must deliver on this commitment. So let’s support and push Bosnia to develop a true democracy and to comply with the case law of the European Court of Human Rights and its own Constitutional Court, including Republika Srpska, and block any effort undermining the prospect of EU membership. We cannot afford to disappoint Bosnian citizens again. They deserve a peaceful and inclusive country where their rights are respected, regardless of their background. Let them be able to count on the European values.

Name: Kinga Gál
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Bosnia and Herzegovina needs substantial support, and the best tool for this is to accelerate the enlargement process. This is how we can pay tribute to the memory of the Srebrenica victims and do the most to ensure that similar atrocities never happen again.

Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: 2016 was the year of submitting the membership application, and finally, in December of last year, this long-awaited path was achieved...Democratic transformation and the rule of law are a good and genuine path for Bosnia and Herzegovina towards its full European integration.

Name: Tonino Picula
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Therefore, we need to consistently apply the conditionality policy, which is part of the IPA III Agreement and the recommendations of the new enlargement strategy of the European Union. Any real progress on this path will have our full support.

Name: Karen Melchior
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: It also marks all of our European populations because in each of our countries we have families that sought refuge as refugees after the genocide or before the genocide and reside in our countries. Name: Ladislav Ilčić
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Bosnia and Herzegovina deserves a European perspective. Name: Bernhard Zimniok
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: In recent years, Bosnia and Herzegovina has received billions from the EU to bring the country up to EU standards. Name: Matjaž Nemec
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)

Name: Tomislav Sokol
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: In this way, and by removing the blockade on forming the executive government in the Federation, the influence of anti-European fundamentalist forces in Sarajevo has been reduced, allowing Bosnia and Herzegovina to truly move towards European integration. Quote: I also want to add my voice in support of Bosnia and Herzegovina's membership in the European Union, but we must describe more strongly the problems associated with President Dodik's political activities. The crisis surrounding the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina, separatist tendencies, and leaning towards Russia have been mentioned multiple times during today's debate. We must not underestimate these issues...I join my colleagues who have clearly stated today that there is a need for sanction mechanisms, sanctions against Dodik and his people. We need to respond decisively to this. This is the only chance to pave the way for Bosnia and Herzegovina's future membership in the European Union. If we close our eyes, the Dodiks will prevail, and Bosnia and Herzegovina will never become a member of the European Union.

Name: Isabel Santos
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Given the level of commitment and responsiveness demonstrated, and the need to make up for lost time due to external issues, this report sets the year 2030 as the target for completing the accession process...It is crucial to continue on the path of reforms in the areas of rule of law and justice, to recover from delays caused by the decrease in human resources resulting from the vetting process, and to improve citizens' access to justice. The fight against corruption and organized crime cannot afford any respite and presents constant challenges...In terms of foreign policy, at this critical juncture, we must not forget that Albania has proven to be a reliable partner aligned with the European Union's Common Foreign and Security Policy, including its role as a member of the UN Security Council...While reforms are underway, it is time to move beyond mere compliance with commitments. It is time to do more and better, and to build an inspiring vision around Albania's European future.

Name: Olivér Várhelyi
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: nearly a year ago we opened accession negotiations with Albania. This was a major step for the country and a clear recognition of Albania’s progress in advancing on its EU reform agenda...We took positive note that the recent local elections on 14 May were held in calm and transparent manner on the day of the vote...The Commission encourages the Albanian authorities to address all outstanding recommendations of the OSCE/ODIHR, as well as from the Venice Commission in this regard...The Commission concluded in last year’s report that the functioning of the judiciary in Albania is moderately prepared. Albania’s legislative and institutional framework on judiciary has a high level of alignment with the EU acquis and European standards...On fundamental rights, Albania maintained overall a positive direction, with an overall robust legislative framework in place. However, there is still a need to continue progress when it comes to the implementation of the fundamental rights, especially in the areas of minority rights, property rights and media freedom, as well as the protection of personal data. Some progress has also been made on the fight against organised crime and the fight against corruption...Further, let me again commend Albania’s continued alignment with the EU’s restrictive measures and sanctions against Russia, maintaining the 100% alignment to our common foreign and security policy. Albania continues to use its ongoing term in the UN Security Council to respond to the crises along like-minded countries. This proves that Albania has shown its determination to advance on the EU path and is a reliable partner...Albania has come a long way on its path towards the European Union, showing persistence in pursuing difficult reforms in the interests of the Albanian people. We would like to see the country entering the next phase of the accession process.

Name: David Lega
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the EU finally opened the accession talks with Albania, which constitutes one step towards EU membership and a new face in the EU-Albania relations. Becoming a member of the EU is not and should not be a quick or an easy process. The road towards EU membership is one of requirements aimed at guaranteeing democratisation, modernisation, the rule of law, stability and growth in each and every state aspiring for EU membership – and it is vital that the pace of accession should be determined by the reform progress. Regarding Albania, I will highlight a couple of issues that I think are crucial. Firstly, we must commend Albania’s consistent and full alignment with the EU’s foreign policy, including its response to the Russian war of aggression against Ukraine. However, when it comes to the situation inside the country, many reforms are still needed. One issue of concern is the deteriorating situation of the freedom of expression and media freedom. The trend is incompatible with EU integration.

Name: Theresa Bielowski
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Two months ago, the Austrian Federal President visited Tirana and emphasized: Albania has long been part of the European family. Next week, I will travel to Tirana with a delegation and will confidently say the same. The progress report clearly shows: Albania has made significant strides in crucial areas such as justice, administration, and in the fight against organized crime...Yes, there are still reforms to be implemented. There are still steps to be taken, but we will tackle these together. The European Union, as a credible actor and reliable partner, will also fulfill its promises to the citizens of Albania and especially to the younger generation, who place so much hope in EU accession. For them, Europe is the future, and Albania is part of that European future.

Name: Ilhan Kyuchyuk
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Albania has come a long way on its European path and with continued determination to resolve undoubtedly difficult issues. Over the past years, the country has demonstrated steadfast, unwavering and strategic commitment to European Union integration...Furthermore, Albania’s consistent and full alignment with the EU’s foreign and security policy is commendable. The country’s resolute efforts to align its interests with those of the European Union demonstrate a profound understanding of the benefits of cooperation and shared values. The country has maintained a focused approach on EU-related reforms. Of course, there is still work to be done. It is imperative to intensify efforts aimed at improving the functioning of the rule of law and judiciary, and the European Parliament should stand ready to support the country on this journey.

Name: Thomas Waitz
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Albania is a success story, clearly. The vetting process and the juridical reforms have not been seen in this dimension in the Balkans. The full alignment with foreign policy and security policy was mentioned by many colleagues already. But I think Albania has a crucial role to play also in stabilising the region. Albania is a stable factor of the region, which is something we cannot say of too many countries of the Western Balkans. Albania has shown real will to reform towards a European Union accession...And yes, also Albania still has a lot of reforms to do and implement a lot of legislation, European legislation. The report is pointing out on some weaknesses that we still see on segregation of parts of the minorities, on media freedom and, you know, fighting disinformation and cutting media freedom is a thin line, so one should not be used to do the other.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Nevertheless, Albania must continue reforms in the area of fundamental rights, rule of law, and justice to make rapid progress on its path towards the European Union. Plans for a fiscal amnesty that would allow up to 2 million euros to be deposited into an Albanian bank account without disclosing the origin of the funds are cause for concern. Albania can and must demonstrate that it cannot be suspected of being a center for shady deals in Europe, and Tirana must clearly show that it is determined to address this issue and not allow the country to become a shield for illegal activities under the guise of new policies. Only swift reforms and decisive steps in combating corruption and organized crime will lead to the rapid conclusion of the negotiation process...At the end of the day, Albania deserves to be a member of the European Union because it has completed its homework, supports pan-European policies, and ultimately shares what even someone like me understands as European values.

Name: Anna Bonfrisco
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: the European Union and Albania share a common destiny, and today we reaffirm the integration aspirations of a friendly and allied state. However, I would like to seize this opportunity to underline Albania's contribution to international peace and stability, the safeguarding of the rule of law among nations, and the preservation of multilateralism. Through its skilled ambassador to the United Nations, Albania has addressed increasingly intense and unstable geopolitical rivalries in the highest forum of multilateralism over the past two years...Italy, with its historical brotherhood with Albania, has the task of increasingly supporting the virtuous process of two countries sharing a sea.

Name: Fabio Massimo Castaldo
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: we finally have reached a significant milestone with the official start of the accession talks and acknowledgment of the remarkable progress Albania has made in advancing the EU reform agenda. Tirana has consistently demonstrated unwavering commitment to EU integration, both in the political and the public domain. I commend the report for acknowledging this dedication, while also highlighting areas that require further attention and efforts, particularly the fight against corruption and media freedom...It is not by chance that the candidate countries, including Albania, have been particularly targeted by Russian disinformation and hybrid attacks. We have demonstrated in practice, and not just in words, our resolute commitment to enlargement, avoiding further factious delays that undermine our credibility and frustrate our partners.

Name: Fabio Massimo Castaldo
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Dear colleagues, recent events, especially the criminal aggression in Ukraine, have emphasised once again an obvious truth – strength lies in unity. Now more than ever, the completion of the EU enlargement in the Western Balkans has become a strategic priority for the future of our Union.

Name: Manolis Kefalogiannis
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: beyond any doubt, Albania's place is in the core of the European family...I also want to emphasize that this issue is closely linked to the respect for fundamental rights, the property issue of the Greek minority in the municipality of Himara, and the allegations of illegal expropriations by the Albanian authorities. The Fredy Beleri case is a blow to the rule of law and to Albania's efforts to align with the European acquis. We expect the immediate release of the only minority mayor, the mayor of Himara, Fredy Beleri.

Name: Andreas Schieder
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Over the past decade, Albania has implemented a tremendous number of reforms – bureaucratic reforms, rule of law reforms, judicial reforms, the fight against corruption, and even at the local level, such as in Tirana, where concrete measures have significantly improved quality of life and urban development. Having said that, one might ask: Is everything perfect? No. Albania still needs to undertake many more reforms. Environmental issues, climate concerns, and sustainability are major topics, as well as labor rights and unions. But one thing is clear: Cooperation with Albania, especially in the context of enlargement, is effectively driving important reforms forward in a professional manner.

Name: Vlad-Marius Botoş
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Albania is moving towards a stable political regime and is becoming a European democracy. There are still issues that need to be addressed and improvements to be made, but it is clear that the country is committed to becoming a strong democracy...A free press is also necessary to highlight deviations from democratic values without fear of consequences. However, none of these challenges should prevent us from recognizing that it is time for Albania to become a member of the European Union. We must move beyond the point where the European Union seems frozen by the fears of extremist parties that reject any opening and any new accession. We have started an accession process that both parties must respect, and I strongly believe that it is time for Albania to join our great European Union family.

Name: Emmanouil Fragkos
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Albania is obliged to treat the Greek national minority of Northern Epirus with respect. Let some understand this well. Albania's path to Europe passes through Korytsa, through the Forty Saints and through Himara. We hear our Northern Epirotes and say "no to Albania in the European Union". Until Fredi Beleri is liberated, they should not even think about Europe. Until he fully assumes his duties as mayor, we call on Europe to impose strict economic sanctions on Albania, because at this moment it is closer to Turkey than to Europe.

Name: Dominique Bilde
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: This country is knocking at the doors of the European Union with cash in hand, as evidenced by the allocation of 758 million euros between 2014 and 2020 alone under the Instrument for Pre-accession Assistance. However, between 2010 and 2019, over 193,000 Albanians applied for asylum in the European Union for reasons that were particularly alarming – from vendettas to human trafficking – in order to be considered refugees. Last year, these same Albanians were among those boarding makeshift boats to cross the English Channel before Rishi Sunak intervened. Is this the standard of a future EU member state? I would also add that with a minimum wage hovering around 360 euros, Albania represents fierce competition, for example in the garment sector, at a time when the Commission claims to be unfolding a sustainability strategy for this industry, and local production is timidly re-emerging in my region of Lorraine, France. Therefore, I am staunchly opposed to any enlargement that would be an economic and civilizational aberration.

Name: Javier Zarzalejos
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I believe we must express our satisfaction with the progress made in Albania towards closer European integration and, ultimately, its accession to the Union as desired by the Albanian people. However, we are aware that this process demands efforts, requires firm commitments, and we cannot ignore the significant deficits in institutional organization, rule of law, electoral legislation, police, justice, and freedoms of expression and assembly.

Name: Nikos Papandreou
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Yes, I agree with what Commissioner and Ms. Santos said; Albania has progressed, but it has lagged significantly in one aspect: Two days before the national elections, it cannot be imprisoning a number of mayors, including the very sensitive issue for us, the mayor of Himara, Freddie Beleri. He was ultimately elected from prison. We demand his release if Albania wants the support of Greece and all of us in its effort to reach Europe by '20 and '30 — and we hope for it. We want all the Western Balkans to join at some point. It must adhere to the rule of law as soon as possible, implement Chapters 23 and 24, and then it will have our applause.

Name: Georgios Kyrtsos
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: I must say that I do not share the optimism of most colleagues. In my view, the biggest obstacle to Albania's accession to the European Union, as well as other countries in the Western Balkans, is the creation of entrenched regimes that tightly control public life. Rama, reminiscent of Vučić in domestic politics, thankfully not in foreign affairs, controls the media, desires control over the judiciary replacing what Berisha had, handles issues of the Greek minority, such as Beleri, without respect for its rights, has created an alliance of interests that controls the country's economy, and tolerates the role of organized crime...I agree, enlargement is necessary from a strategic perspective, but it must inevitably pass through democratization and respect for the rule of law, without exceptions.

Name: Pascual Navarro Ríos
Type: Member of Council of the EU
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Moldova's context is complex. Russia's aggression against Ukraine has exacerbated a difficult situation, especially in energy, economy, and security. We are encouraged by the strong support from both the Moldovan government and its citizens for implementing reforms and moving towards their European future...The enhancement of security and defense cooperation by Moldova, and the country's contribution to EU missions under the Common Security and Defense Policy, are also highly valued...Regarding enlargement, last June — as I mentioned — the European Council recognized Moldova's determination to meet the nine conditions required in its accession process to the European Union and the enormous efforts it was making towards this goal...I will just mention that the progress made regarding some reform measures has been very positive, and the Council encourages Moldova to accelerate the reform process, particularly in combating corruption, fighting organized crime, and reforming public administration, especially in light of the upcoming enlargement package that the Commission will soon present. The accession process is, and will continue to be, based on fulfilling conditions and merit for each candidate. Therefore, the Presidency awaits the Commission's upcoming enlargement package and its comprehensive report on Moldova's progress in its reform process to proceed with the established procedures.

Name: Janez Lenarčič
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: the future of Moldova is in our Union...During the past year, Moldova has made good progress on its European path...We commend the Government’s continued commitment to Moldova’s EU path. This has by now translated into further progress in key areas such as judicial reform, fighting corruption, organised crime and money laundering, and pursuing important reforms...Later in the autumn, the Commission will present the annual enlargement package. For the first time, it will comprise an assessment of Moldova’s overall progress as a candidate country, including the implementation of the nine reform steps. On that basis, EU Member States will be able to take informed decisions on further steps on Moldova’s EU path.

Name: Andrzej Halicki
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I would like to start with the conclusion because I would like to call in the name of the European People’s Party, the European Council, to open the accession process at talks during the planned in December meeting until the end of the year. It’s really expected. It’s high time to give the clear message to the citizens of Moldova. We all are impressed of implementation of the reforms and working also together in this House over the political splits on this goal, which is expected. Moldova is in Europe. Moldova’s inhabitants are Europeans. This is obvious for us.

Name: Thijs Reuten
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: What I admire most in Moldova is that, unlike any other candidate countries, it is very open about the outstanding issues, the things still requiring a lot of work. No overly rosy picture, but an honest account of what will require more time, but with the firm political will to get the job done. Let us shore up technical support, increase security cooperation and make sure that, through accelerating judicial reform and closer alignment with our internal market, the Moldovan people will experience concrete improvements way ahead of the EU membership they deserve. Moldova is Europe.

Name: Dragoş Tudorache
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: the Republic of Moldova must be given the green light for opening EU accession talks...Of course, there are tough reforms that Moldova must go through in its economy, in its judiciary, in all branches of its administration, and the Moldovan authorities have demonstrated against impossible odds, and under continuous pressure and hybrid warfare from Putin’s Russia that they have the political will and executive stamina to deliver on these reforms. They have taken concrete steps in bringing oligarchs their empires down. They started clearing up the judiciary of corruption and incompetence...That is what we must do, that is what being geopolitical is all about. This is how we best tell Putin that his disturbed vision of imperialism will not win in Europe.

Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Russia has tried everything, and the Republic of Moldova has repelled everything. Its democratic, pro-European government remains steadfast, safeguarding the country's future. To every Russian attempt to destabilize the country, our response must be "more Europe for Moldova": more support to reduce inflation and living costs, more backing for democratic processes, more incentives for the economy...The Republic of Moldova's progress on the new recommendations must be acknowledged. Initiating accession talks is the only logical next step. Moldova has earned it by withstanding unimaginable pressure and sheltering hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian refugees. Republic of Moldova: Welcome back, home in Europe!

Name: Anna Fotyga
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: I wholeheartedly congratulate all Moldovans led by their courageous president, Maia Sandu, on their progress to the European Union, and I declare my unwavering support for their European path, hoping for very soon possibility decisions to open negotiations with Moldova. They proceed on their reforms on their way to the European Union, despite enormous – I repeat, enormous – difficulties. And that proves their will to join us as soon as possible. Our will should be similar.

Name: Emmanuel Maurel
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: The inflation rate is very concerning, as are the public debt and deficit, which are not sustainable in the long term...Regarding accession, I must express caution. I am not convinced that Moldova is currently ready to start accession negotiations. I believe any decision to move forward in this regard would be premature and potentially counterproductive, given the political, administrative, and judicial structures in Moldova, where endemic corruption remains a serious issue and adaptation cannot occur as quickly as we might hope. What Moldovans primarily need is assistance. I believe we can understand and act on this together, especially in the realm of energy. However, when it comes to enlargement, I urge my colleagues not to create the impression of rushing forward. It seems that Europe, uncertain of its direction, has adopted a principle of continual enlargement without fundamentally questioning the reasons behind it. Additionally, there is significant intra-European competition and social dumping, and we must avoid the consequence of this being rejection of Europe by its peoples.

Name: Siegfried Mureșan
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the Republic of Moldova is a candidate country for accession to the European Union. The citizens of the Republic of Moldova aspire to live, just like us, in freedom and democracy. As members of the European Parliament, we must state very clearly: one day, the Republic of Moldova will be a member of the European Union, and Moldovan citizens will have exactly the same rights as all citizens of the other EU member states. We see how reforms, which have been delayed for years in the Republic of Moldova, are finally being implemented swiftly. We see efforts to combat corruption, strengthen justice, and reinforce the rule of law in Moldova...Therefore, through this resolution, we, the European Parliament, will state very clearly: we call for the start of accession negotiations for the Republic of Moldova to the European Union by the end of this year. This way, Moldova will modernize and reform even further, as quickly as possible — a good thing for the citizens of Moldova and for the people of the European Union.

Name: Juozas Olekas
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Today, the European Parliament's resolution rightly acknowledges Moldova's progress in implementing reforms and demonstrating strong commitments to joining the community of European nations. I am pleased with the Moldovan people's choice and the mandate given to the pro-European Moldovan government to carry out necessary reforms. I understand that the path of reforms is neither easy nor quick, especially when the country hosts one of the largest numbers of Ukrainian refugees relative to its population...I have no doubt that in a few weeks, the European Commission will positively assess Moldova's progress, and in December, the Council will make a positive decision to start accession negotiations with the European Union. Moldova is Europe.

Name: Petras Auštrevičius
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: the Republic of Moldova’s future is closely linked to full membership of the European Union. At this point in time, it is essential, on the one hand, to continue and complete the reform of state institutions and to strengthen them, and, on the other hand, to increase Moldova’s resilience to threats from Russia...We must continue to give our full support and assistance to the democratic government and people of Moldova in meeting these challenges. More importantly, we must open EU accession negotiations with Moldova by the end of this year.

Name: Markéta Gregorová
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: I am very pleased to see that the relationship between the EU and Moldova is strengthening...Additionally, I welcome Moldova's efforts towards judicial reform, civil society engagement and gender equality and overall positive signals from the Commission regarding the nine recommendations’ implementation. However, there is still much more work to be done as implementing deep structural reforms is essential for alignment with the EU standards. Moldova must step up, notably in fighting corruption, organised crime and public administration reforms. Overall, I appreciate the new EU enlargement momentum in this political term. Nevertheless, it is crucial that the Member States deliver on their promises in the accession processes for those who wish to join our European family.

Name: Cristian Terheş
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: Although the legal border of the EU in the East currently stops due to the perpetuation of the Ribbentrop-Molotov Pact's effect, the natural place for Moldova is alongside Romania in the EU. The citizens of Moldova have shown affinity towards the values of the free world, refusing to yield to Russia's blackmail, whether through economic, hybrid, or military means. Therefore, I call on the European Commission to continue supporting Moldova's integration and to initiate accession negotiations promptly.

Name: Helmut Scholz
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: Moldova has been a candidate country for accession to the European Union for almost 16 months now, and it is important that we discuss today the path that still lies ahead...However, we must remain honest. The hurdles that the country still needs to overcome are significant. From finding a sustainable solution for Transnistria, to tackling endemic corruption, reforming the judiciary, ensuring an inclusive, plural democracy, especially in the face of the frozen Transnistrian conflict and Russian aggression in Ukraine with its regional and international implications, to ensuring media freedom and a discrimination-free life for Roma, LGBTQ+ individuals, and others — there is still much work to be done.

Name: David McAllister
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: President Maia Sandu and her pro-European government are operating in constant crisis mode. And yet, they have succeeded in introducing key legislative initiatives tailored to the nine conditions set by the European Commission. These are tremendous efforts. Soon, the Commission’s upcoming enlargement package will testify to these reforms...Moldova’s entry into the European Single Market would boost exports, attract investments and foster integration with the European Union. And colleagues, both parties would benefit from starting EU accession negotiations. The citizens of Moldova deserve the perspective of joining our European Union.

Name: Margarida Marques
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: I recently had the opportunity to visit Moldova on a mission of the European Parliament and witnessed the commitment and political will towards implementing reforms and integrating the EU acquis...We await the European Commission's report on the enlargement package for 2023. It is crucial that Moldova fulfills the nine steps identified by the European Commission as necessary for opening negotiations. Moldova should continue steadfastly with its reform agenda concerning democracy, rule of law, respect for human rights, respect and protection of minorities, combating organized crime and corruption, and efforts to enhance the country's energy security.

Name: Vlad-Marius Botoş
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The Republic of Moldova has obtained candidate status for the European Union following an intense campaign of democratization and reforms, supported by the sustained efforts of President Maia Sandu. The determination of our neighbors to adopt the European path is evident, even through the adoption of organizational models for national institutions and programs, such as the Local Action Groups implemented in Moldova following the European Union's model. It is crucial that these efforts continue, and the country fulfills the European acquis as soon as possible. However, European commitment must also be commensurate, and once Moldova meets its obligations, it should be accepted as a full member of the European Union.

Name: Adam Bielan
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: the authorities and institutions of Moldova have recently been conducting a highly ambitious reform programme, driving the country towards greater transparency, democracy and political stability...We also emphasised today the importance of Moldova’s integration within the EU. We must continue supporting its people and grant the country access to vital EU programmes and instruments...The story of Moldova is one of resilience in turbulent times. Let us truly acknowledge this and continue the work to welcome Moldova in the EU, where it belongs.

Name: Andrius Kubilius
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Moldova is not only the country which is showing great strength in reforming itself, in building a successful democratic country, but also is a litmus test for us, for the EU itself. It’s obvious that Moldova and Ukraine deserve to be invited at the end of this year to start negotiations for the membership in EU. That would be the major step forward and that is needed not only for Moldova or Ukraine, but for the EU itself. Those countries cannot be left anymore in the ‘grey geopolitical’ zone, because such an EU approach to Moldova and Ukraine during the last decades created temptation for Putin to start a military invasion into Ukraine. That is why it is important not only to start negotiations, it is very important to have an ambitious agenda to conclude negotiations within the next three or four years

Name: Andrius Kubilius
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: It’s obvious that Moldova and Ukraine deserve to be invited at the end of this year to start negotiations for the membership in EU. That would be the major step forward and that is needed not only for Moldova or Ukraine, but for the EU itself. Those countries cannot be left anymore in the ‘grey geopolitical’ zone, because such an EU approach to Moldova and Ukraine during the last decades created temptation for Putin to start a military invasion into Ukraine. That is why it is important not only to start negotiations, it is very important to have an ambitious agenda to conclude negotiations within the next three or four years

Name: Victor Negrescu
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: The Republic of Moldova is ready to take a step forward towards the European Union, and this must be confirmed by a positive report from the European Commission this autumn, which should swiftly initiate accession negotiations with the European Union...This means that efforts to create new economic links in energy, culture, and education, which limit the influence of the Russian Federation, represent real solutions to support Moldova's European path. After decades of propaganda, the battle for the minds and values of Moldovans is still ongoing. Let's win it decisively!

Name: Dacian Cioloş
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Beyond the discussions we are having here about administrative procedures and political positioning to bring Moldova into the European Union, it is crucial that the accession process to the EU is felt positively by the citizens of the Republic of Moldova...Dear friends, this is and will be your home too. Until the moment of signing on the accession treaty, the most important thing is that Moldova is already becoming part of the European family in several sectors.

Name: Ryszard Czarnecki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)
Quote: I have been to Moldova several times, a country that shares historical ties with Poland dating back centuries. I believe that what is happening there is actually a very important geopolitical game between the West and Russia. Moldova deserves our full support, serious support...To President Sandu, I have this good advice: focus on your country's accession to the European Union

Name: Alexander Alexandrov Yordanov
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: active support for the European integration of the Republic of Moldova is necessary. Russia is the major obstacle in front of it. That is why we must firmly support the decisions of the government and President Maia Sandu to refuse cooperation with Russia in all areas. It is necessary to impose new sanctions on individuals and organizations serving Russian interests. The citizens of Moldova must feel the benefits of their European choice throughout the entire European integration process. Every day, month, and year of their lives should truly become European.

Name: Corina Crețu
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: the Republic of Moldova has strongly expressed its desire to belong to the European family, steadfast in the face of hybrid attacks from Russia, coping with multiple crises, and welcoming the largest number of Ukrainian refugees relative to its population. Just as my grandparents were welcomed by Romania, together with 400,000 other citizens who fled Bessarabia between 1940 and 1944, when my mother was two years old. I was in Chișinău last week, and I assure you that the Republic of Moldova is ready to start accession negotiations immediately at the beginning of next year...I believe it is time to rise to the occasion of this historical moment, not to miss the opportunity for these citizens to live where they wish and where they belong: in the European Union.

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Moldova always was Europe and Moldova belongs in Europe. I trust that the Commission will propose to start accession negotiations. Thanks to the leadership of President Maia Sandu and the current Government, Moldova has proved that it is a resilient democracy...The EU must stand by Moldova and continue assisting its energy independence, modernisation and integration into EU. And, most important, with Moldova in the EU, Europe – all of us – will be stronger and more secure.

Name: Maria Grapini
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Moldova must follow the European path, and if necessary, we must support it. And it's not just about funds. I am a member of the Delegation for Moldova, I know Moldova very well, I go there frequently. They also need technical support because administrative reform primarily requires human resources...I urge the Commission, as I have done before, in addition to financial support, to provide this technical assistance so that reforms can be implemented and yes, Moldova can start its path towards EU accession. There is no other way for Moldova.

Name: Jiří Pospíšil
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: I am delighted that across all political groups, virtually all speakers have supported the accelerated accession of Moldova to the European Union. I welcome this greatly. I believe it is extraordinarily important that we cannot leave this country in limbo, thereby creating space for Russia to strengthen its influence there. Initiating the next phase of negotiations with Moldova as early as next year, in my opinion, is extraordinarily important. It is not only in the interest of Moldova, which cares for refugees, but also in our interest to prevent the creation of a buffer zone of states between Putin's Russia and the European Union, states that would be demoralized by the delay of their EU accession.

Name: Dan-Ștefan Motreanu
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Moldova's place is within the European Union, and I hereby reiterate the European Parliament's call to the Commission and the Council to commence accession negotiations with the Republic of Moldova by the end of 2023. I emphasize the importance of the Moldovan government's ongoing reform process in not only achieving the political objective of EU accession but primarily improving the country's economic and social situation to provide younger generations with attractive prospects for living and working in their homeland.

Name: Mihai Tudose
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: I support the resolution urging the European Commission and Council to commence negotiations with the Republic of Moldova for accession to the European Union by the end of this year. The report highlights Moldova's efforts and significant progress in pursuing reforms.

Name: Tonino Picula
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: I expected and hoped that my final speech on the situation in the country in this mandate would begin with congratulations to Podgorica on concluding long, demanding, and exhausting membership negotiations and that we would celebrate together the closure of all negotiation chapters. Unfortunately, the current situation has largely disillusioned my expectations, and not only mine. Montenegro has, admittedly, opened all negotiation chapters, but none of them have been closed in the last six years...Regarding the content of the report itself, positive aspects should be commended. Montenegro is fully aligned with the European Union's common foreign policy, including sanctions against Russia, and we certainly appreciate this. We also welcome the appointment of three new judges to the Constitutional Court as a step towards resolving the constitutional crisis. We take note of improvements in anti-corruption efforts and the positive trend in the work of the Agency for the Prevention of Corruption...All these positive steps would mean much more if parallel efforts were made to address systemic problems, primarily those identified in the benchmarks in Chapters 23 and 24.

Name: Olivér Várhelyi
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Montenegro was considered by many to be the most advanced negotiating country. However, it has lost focus in recent years and opportunities have been missed. Precious time is being lost. We agree with the House that Montenegro needs to move forward...It is in our common interest to speed up the enlargement process. The process continues to be built on strict, but fair, conditionality and the principle of own merits. This means that the pace of negotiations depends, first and foremost, on the progress on fundamental reforms. There is a window of opportunity for those countries willing to speed up the pace of their reforms and clearly demonstrate their commitment to EU values, not only in words but also in deeds.

Name: Vladimír Bilčík
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)

So today, more than ever, politicians in Podgorica have an historic opportunity to move forward decisively on the European path...The report underlines the key tasks ahead: to continue the support to Ukraine, to deliver on rule of law reforms, as well as electoral changes, to fight corruption and organised crime, to safeguard free and independent media, to protect minorities and women’s rights...This is why I want to call on all truly pro-European politicians to act responsibly and in the interests of the people of Montenegro. Please keep your country on the EU path. Only if you do so can we engage and deliver on EU membership for Montenegro in the very near future.

Name: Matjaž Nemec
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Montenegro, which until recently was considered the leading country in the Western Balkans in its approach to the European Union, is now experiencing a deep political and institutional crisis. High political tensions and polarization over the years have slowly but continuously weakened the Montenegrin engine that drives the country forward in key reforms. Additionally, it must be acknowledged that the country has become a battleground for the unabashed expression of external interests and is struggling with the influences of other countries from the region and beyond, which has further pushed Montenegro into stagnation in implementing key reforms. And this is unacceptable. Despite the current situation, I remain optimistic...My optimism is also fueled by the 33 open chapters and, not least, by the political turnaround in the summer elections.

Name: Klemen Grošelj
Party: Renew Europe (RE)

The worst part is that while the rhetoric in the EU regarding enlargement is changing and decisions are being made to encourage countries in the region to carry out necessary reforms, aside from cosmetic adjustments, the necessary progress is still not happening...However, a significant part of the blame also lies with the countries of the region themselves, and Montenegro is unfortunately no exception. Why? It has allowed itself, due to internal political and other polarizations, to slip from being a leader in the Western Balkans to just another country in the region. Nevertheless, Montenegro has the opportunity to be a candidate that could join the EU even before the magical year 2030. To achieve this, Montenegrin politics must overcome ideological, political, and other grievances and focus more on the European future of the country rather than fears and delusions of the past and counting the population. The decision is simple yet crucial. It is a choice between the future or a return to the past.

Name: Thomas Waitz
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)

It has had some progress when it came to fulfilling chapter 23 and chapter 24 requirements when it comes to judges. But we also see a country where the obvious common willingness to join the European Union has not really shaped the political decision making. And I really call on Montenegro that is still the frontrunner in the negotiations. I call on Montenegrin politicians when it comes to the questions of accession, of fulfilling chapters 23 and 24, to leave aside their disputes and look into the actual future of their country and deliver on the future of their country and the will of their populations, to bring Montenegro closer to entering the European Union.

Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)

And that is that the Yugoslav legacy, the communist legacy, the Bolshevik legacy, the Kremlin Russian legacy, hinder the people in this region from continuing their deserved and normal pro-European path, which can and should be encouraged. Without the elimination of Belgrade, without the elimination of the Kremlin, this will be very difficult to achieve and you know it very well.

I encourage Montenegro to work on good neighborly relations, to resolve border issues, to shed light on war crimes, and to investigate the fate of the missing.

Name: Viola von Cramon-Taubadel
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: EU enlargement is a moment of truth for Europe. Our investment in enlargement today will make us more independent and secure tomorrow. I would like to underline two guiding principles for that endeavour. Firstly, enlarging our Union is EU’s geopolitical necessity, but it is also a geopolitical choice, a choice that must be loud and clear; a choice, in the case of the Serbian President, which is incompatible with authoritarian tendency in cosying-up with Beijing and Moscow. Secondly, Copenhagen criteria entail the process and progress based on merits. This means making sure that the judiciary plays an independent role in fighting corruption and organised crime, and standing with us in foreign policy – more important today than ever. Dear friends in the Western Balkans, in Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia: enlargement is a choice for us, but also a choice to you. So it is up to you to move forward with credible reforms as the EU has finally woken up to the call of history.

Name: Anders Vistisen
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: Has anyone learned from the chaos that the eastward enlargement brought, precisely because the agreed rules were not adhered to? We have seen a wave of social dumping. We have seen a wave of organized crime. Yes, even today – 15 years after our last major enlargement – several member states still do not have access to the Schengen cooperation, still do not have access to the euro area because they are not yet ready. And in this situation, they are talking about expanding the EU by up to 55 million new inhabitants, all coming from countries that are even poorer and have an even worse rule of law situation than Poland and Hungary, which this house loves to criticize. So when does the hypocrisy stop?

Name: Emmanuel Maurel
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: I understand the peoples who wish to join the European Union, starting with the Ukrainian people who are under aggression, and we stand in solidarity with them. I understand my sincere colleagues in this chamber who believe that it is our moral duty to welcome them and that it is also necessary from a geopolitical perspective. But against the evidence, I ask the question: are we ready to absorb such a shock? Are the economic and political conditions met? I believe not. You have mentioned the political conditions: the countries in question obviously do not meet the Copenhagen criteria. But there is also our own situation: the economic crisis we are facing, the social crisis, the explosion of inequalities. And I am not sure that European workers are ready to pay for a new enlargement, both because of budgetary transfers and social dumping. I urge you to think about this: Europe is a very fragile construction, and I am not sure that today we are ready to absorb an additional 50 million inhabitants into the European Union.

Name: Ernő Schaller-Baross
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: if we want a strong Europe, our enlargement policy must take into account our geopolitical and security needs. The European Union should not view enlargement as a tool for coercion or appeasement, nor should it apply double standards in the accession process, thereby undermining its own unity and credibility. I urge us to refrain from such practices. Countries aspiring to join the European Union must comply with the conditions set forth in the laws, especially the Copenhagen criteria. These conditions should be uniform and equal for all countries seeking accession. It not only undermines trust but also the geostrategic interests of EU member states that certain countries in the Western Balkans have been led on for over a decade without significant progress, while Ukraine is being pushed forward with accelerated enlargement policies. Our request is simple: apply the same rules to everyone.

Name: Andrey Kovatchev
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the unity of our continent based on our common European values is the most important condition for our security and prosperity. The transformative power of the European Union must be renewed every day with clear plans and timelines for the accession of new member states. Where we leave a gray area in Europe, Russia will attempt to fill it. Ukrainians have felt this on their backs based on our major mistake of not accepting them into NATO at that time. The full integration of these countries into our Union is imperative as a geostrategic investment in a stable, strong, and united Europe. Of course, integration is a two-way street and candidate countries must overcome the problems inherited from the past. Achieving historic reconciliation, overcoming hate speech, and nondiscrimination against all citizens, regardless of how they self-identify, is fair and a fundamental value of the European Union.

Name: Alessandra Moretti
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: In these 30 years, much has changed in Europe and around the world, but one thing has remained the same: enlargement policy remains one of the most important tools to ensure peace, security, and prosperity for peoples. The Russian aggression against Ukraine aims to weaken the enlargement and accession process, potentially pushing countries near our borders into the arms of authoritarian regimes. Therefore, I address the Western Balkans, particularly Serbia, urging them to continue their accession process to strengthen the rule of law, solidarity, and common growth through a clear and unambiguous path.

Name: Jean-Lin Lacapelle
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: the Copenhagen criteria, which are celebrating their 30th anniversary, consist of a set of criteria related to economic health, stability, and respect for democracy, which all countries wishing to join the European Union must strictly adhere to. So, I take you at your word. Where is the stability in Ukraine, attacked by Russia? Where is the stability in Moldova, with the Transnistria region that has seceded with 20,000 tons of weapons? Where is the respect for democracy in Kosovo, which persecutes the Serbian minority? Where is the economic prosperity when most of the Balkans suffer from enormous poverty and massive corruption? Where is the social economy in Albania, plagued by arms, drug, and prostitution trafficking? Where is democracy in Turkey, where journalists are imprisoned and opponents oppressed? Enough with the hypocrisy... These criteria are actually variable, ideological, secondary once the European Union has decided it wants to continue its expansionist project, but terribly disastrous for the future of Europe.

Name: Vladimír Bilčík
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Today, the Copenhagen criteria are as relevant as ever. After Russia’s brutal aggression against Ukraine, there is a strong political will across Europe to enlarge further in our east neighbourhood and in the Western Balkans. Yet, just like in the past, there can be no shortcuts for the accession countries. They do have to adapt to the EU’s democratic and rule of law principles. And, at the same time, we in the EU must reform ourselves in order to prepare for new Member States. The next enlargement can succeed if we all again rediscover the meaning, the power and the benefits of the Copenhagen criteria. Dear colleagues, enlargement takes hard work, but it pays off.

Name: Francisco José Millán Mon
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Firstly, it is evident that Article 49 of the Treaty and the Copenhagen criteria must be adhered to. Enlargement is an individual process based on the merits of each country. The delay of one candidate should not mean that other countries have to postpone their accession, and setting fixed dates seems inappropriate. We cannot accelerate timelines, allow shortcuts, or create false expectations.

Name: Rovana Plumb
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: European Union enlargement is not just about admitting new member states, about the acquis communautaire, or the Copenhagen criteria. EU enlargement is about realizing the potential of the European Union, about positioning ourselves on the world map at a time of great tensions and strategic competitions. It is about people and the values they embrace. We are at a turning point in history and we must have the strength to make the right choices, as well as to undertake the efforts necessary to implement these decisions. Moldova, Georgia, the Western Balkans, and Ukraine have chosen the European path. These people, in many cases, have paid the price for their choice with blood. The enlargement package proposed by the European Commission is the right gesture at the right time and has our full support.
