Name: Željana Zovko
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Expansion is essential for our physical defense against threats from those using the vacuum we left behind. Lastly, open negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina; everything started with it.

Name: Željana Zovko
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Lastly, open negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina; everything started with it.

Name: Matjaž Nemec
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Twenty years ago, we extended the European perspective to the Western Balkans. However, all too often nowadays, it seems we have forgotten both promises. The Copenhagen criteria are violated by existing member states. The enlargement policy has been stagnant for many years, so in the face of heightened geopolitical conditions in our neighborhood, both commitments are not only politically courageous but strategically necessary. Despite all its challenges, the enlargement policy remains the greatest guarantee of peace, security, and stability. However, it also brings numerous challenges and pitfalls that the European Union must urgently resolve before future enlargements. Therefore, esteemed colleagues, Europe will never be complete and perfect without the Western Balkans in its family. We have the capability to achieve this! We have a moral duty to fulfill this commitment.

Name: Petras Auštrevičius
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The significance of the Copenhagen criteria has not diminished to this day. Of course, they are influenced by the new geopolitical situation and the strategic factors that arise from it. The Copenhagen criteria established objective parameters for membership, creating opportunities for candidate countries to be compared and engage in constructive competition. Dear colleagues, let us not forget the political history of our continent, and let us not be afraid to walk the path towards a united Europe.

Name: Tomislav Sokol
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: the Copenhagen criteria still represent the key conditions that candidate countries must fulfill to become members of the European Union. After a prolonged period of enlargement fatigue, it seems that there is finally political will emerging to continue this political process. If the European Union does not offer clear perspectives to its neighboring countries, they will fall completely under the influence of foreign powers, which in the long term represents a catastrophe for Europe's security. Let's be clear: in the enlargement process, each country must be assessed individually and judged on its own merits

Name: Tomislav Sokol
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: There is no skipping the line to EU accession. This especially must be understood by Aleksandar Vučić, under whose rule Serbian hegemonism has become the main threat to the stability of Southeast Europe. Moreover, democracy in Serbia has not just stalled; it has regressed significantly.

Name: Tomislav Sokol
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: On the other hand, the European Commission's decision to conditionally recommend the opening of accession negotiations for Bosnia and Herzegovina is an encouragement for that country to continue its reform process, which should be welcomed and supported amidst the difficult reforms it faces.

Name: Barry Andrews
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The criteria is the way we will build our European home, but we mustn’t allow Putin, in particular, to get away with weaponising the Copenhagen criteria through the seeding of conflict in neighbours and the enragement and inflaming of minority sentiment. That is why I fully endorse the decision to provide a clear pathway to membership for both Ukraine and Moldova.

Name: Barry Andrews
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The criteria is the way we will build our European home, but we mustn’t allow Putin, in particular, to get away with weaponising the Copenhagen criteria through the seeding of conflict in neighbours and the enragement and inflaming of minority sentiment. That is why I fully endorse the decision to provide a clear pathway to membership for both Ukraine and Moldova.

Name: Dubravka Šuica
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: I look forward to cooperating closely with our partners on meeting the Copenhagen criteria and working towards an enlarged Union. The European project is not complete without our partners from the Western Balkans and the East. The Copenhagen criteria will continue to guide us on this journey towards an enlarged European Union.

Name: Dubravka Šuica
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: I look forward to cooperating closely with our partners on meeting the Copenhagen criteria and working towards an enlarged Union. The European project is not complete without our partners from the Western Balkans and the East. The Copenhagen criteria will continue to guide us on this journey towards an enlarged European Union.

Name: Andrea Bocskor
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: The Copenhagen criteria were established to ensure the enlargement of the European Union is based on unified principles and values. The goal of enlargement should be to strengthen the Union strategically and ensure its peace and security. It is crucial to avoid making EU accession empty promises for aspiring countries. However, recent years have shown that the EU's enlargement policy is characterized by double standards: while Western Balkan countries have been fulfilling requirements for accession for years without progress, Ukraine is advancing rapidly.

Name: Andrea Bocskor
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Ukraine submitted its accession application shortly after the outbreak of war, committing to EU values and undertaking the reforms proposed by the Union. Nevertheless, some of these reforms are merely superficial actions: Ukraine, under the guise of its reform program, has enacted laws that restrict minority rights, depriving national minorities with ties to European mother countries of their previously acquired rights. An example of this is Ukraine's new law on national minorities replacing the 1992 Minority Law, which represents a setback in the exercise of rights for minorities in the country. Ukraine's EU accession can only be supported if it fully implements the Union's accession conditions! It is crucial that peace prevails in Ukraine and serious efforts are made to restore minority rights!

Name: Roberta Metsola
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The European Parliament was the first to call for Ukraine to receive EU candidate status and we were the strongest advocate for EU accession negotiations to start last year. Because we know that Ukraine’s place is within our Union.

Name: Hadja Lahbib
Type: Member of Council of the EU
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: All our energy, today and tomorrow, must focus on our unity, long-term cohesion, and the European Council's decision to start accession negotiations with Ukraine sends a powerful signal of hope and confidence. It has strengthened Ukraine's European momentum and sends an equally strong signal to Russia: Ukraine's future lies within the Union, and its accession is now only a matter of time – and the clock is ticking.

Name: Ursula von der Leyen
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: Two years ago, Putin and Russia started a war against something, a war against Ukraine and its territory, but also against the people and a nation with an iron will and hope for the future; against their European aspirations; against the values they share with us; and quite simply, against both modern reality and the strong tides of European history...This leads me to my third and last point on Ukraine’s path towards our Union. The contrast with just ten years ago couldn’t be starker. Back then, a pro-Russia regime in Ukraine was passing authoritarian laws and killing protesters on the streets. Today, this country has just given itself new legislation to expand national minority rights, to improve the judicial system, and to ensure checks and balances on power. This is what led us to launching the accession negotiations. This progress is happening not only because Europe is asking for it. This is the deep desire of the people of Ukraine. Ukraine is Europe, because Europe is in the hearts and in the minds of Ukrainians. Soon enough, Ukraine will also be in our Union.

Name: Rasa Juknevičienė
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: But I see such a union only together with Ukraine, with Ukraine, in the EU and in NATO, with its army, which is clearly the strongest army in Europe today. The victory of Ukraine will be the victory of the whole Europe. Only victory can solve the historic eastern dilemma in Europe. Slava Ukraini! Long live Europe!

Name: Jean-Paul Garraud
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: while the situation in Ukraine deserves all attention, it should not lead to detrimental situations for our own nationals. Integrating Ukraine into the European Union would be disastrous for our livestock breeders and farmers, especially in France.

Name: Fabio Massimo Castaldo
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Putin must know that we will not be afraid, we will not hesitate, we will support the Ukrainian people and their sovereignty and freedom with all our strength, and that very soon Ukraine will be our 28th Member State. Because there is no Ukraine without Europe, but there is also no Europe without Ukraine.

Name: Anders Vistisen
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: The mixing of economic aid for Ukraine's war effort and Ukrainian membership of the EU is deeply damaging. The truth is, we do not want to discuss the consequences of Ukrainian EU membership, but I do not wish to participate in concealment and denial. If Ukraine becomes a member of the EU, it will mean more Eastern European crime, more social dumping, more welfare tourism. For Denmark alone, the economic cost would be 26 billion every budget period, equivalent to 5-6 of the so-called super hospitals. And therefore, dear friends, Ukrainian membership of the EU is a cultural and economic disaster for our cooperation.

Name: Lukas Mandl
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: We must stand together, we must stand with Ukraine. We must not give the people of Ukraine false impressions that this will end quickly or that EU membership will come quickly. But Ukraine will be free. Europe will be free, democratic, and based on the rule of law – and every effort is worthwhile for this.

Name: Paulo Rangel
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Without these pillars - financial support, humanitarian support, military support, integration into the European Union, and future integration into NATO - Europe will be weaker, Europe will be vulnerable, and Putin and the Russian invaders will have a victory.

Name: Željana Zovko
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: The European future of Bosnia and Herzegovina hinges on opening negotiations and support in the fight against autocratic regimes and those looking at Putin's path thinking it will pass easily due to conformist hesitation.

Name: Eero Heinäluoma
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Ukraine is fighting under difficult and demanding conditions. Our promise of a European future, EU membership, is crucial in guiding Ukraine forward. While understanding the challenges of war, we trust that the path to EU membership will help Ukraine undertake necessary reforms, commit to democracy and civil liberties, and build a society free from corruption.

Name: Tomáš Zdechovský
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Rape, looting, murder—these are examples of Putin's regime. A regime that threatens not only Ukraine but all of European democracy. Ladies and gentlemen, for two years we have been talking about the need to support Ukraine. So let's do something about it. It's no longer time for useless chatter; it's time for real action. Time to show Ukraine that we keep our word and that we see Ukraine as a future member state of the European Union.

Name: Ivan Štefanec
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: In the European Parliament, we have been strong advocates for Ukraine to attain candidate status for EU membership and for accession negotiations to commence last year. We are entering the third year of Russia's offensive war, and we must continue to firmly stand with Ukraine and its people, who are fighting not only for their freedom but also for our collective security and our shared European values of freedom and democracy. Ukraine's place is in our Union, and therefore, it is time for real action. We must uphold our commitments to Ukraine and support it in achieving the victory that is essential for the whole of Europe.

Name: Pedro Silva Pereira
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: Undoubtedly, the challenges posed by Russia's aggression against Ukraine have underscored the geostrategic importance of enlargement. However, it is not enough to proclaim that enlargement is important; we must ensure the conditions for it to be viable and successful. Therefore, the first message of this report is that enlargement cannot be taken lightly. On the contrary, it must be a demanding process, without shortcuts and predefined timelines. Candidate countries must indeed implement reforms to meet the Copenhagen criteria, with a focus on respect for Union values and fundamental principles, human rights, and the functioning of democracy and the rule of law. Addressing these issues now is better than waiting until it is too late.

Name: Petras Auštrevičius
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: The achievements and ambitions of EU member states inspire others to seek membership and align with it. This is a valid choice, affirmed by real-life changes and their consequences. Let's be open: the changes influenced by EU enlargement, economic prosperity, new societal perspectives, growing international power, and influence only underline the achievements of enlargement policy. Together, we are stronger. The EU's ability to utilize established enlargement negotiation procedures ensures mutually beneficial conditions on an objective basis.

Name: Petras Auštrevičius
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: Currently, we stand on the threshold of a new chapter in European history, beyond which lies the opportunity to fundamentally conclude the European integration process. Eastern European and Western Balkan states can and must replicate past successes in the enlargement process. Candidates aspire. The EU must create clear conditions for engagement in future enlargement processes. The progress demonstrated by candidates in reforms and negotiations is a decisive criterion for accession, but support for fundamental democratic values and the EU's common foreign and security policy is critically important. Candidate states must choose which area of values and security they seek to integrate into.

Party: Renew Europe (RE)

Name: Didier Reynders
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: The Western Balkans, Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia belong to the European family. They are a crucial part of a Europe whole and free. As stated in Parliament’s report, in an increasingly volatile geopolitical context, the political urge of so many countries to join the EU underscores the promise of enlargement and shows that the European Union remains an anchor of peace, prosperity and security...First and foremost, enlargement is and will remain a merit-based process. It requires major efforts by the candidate countries, and for the EU itself, we must show the same determination.

Name: Didier Reynders
Party: Other - Not specified
Quote: A larger Union has greater geopolitical weight and influence on the global stage, including as an economic partner. A larger Union can help reduce critical dependencies and allows it to act more autonomously. A larger Union strengthens the competitiveness and growth potential of the single market, creating new opportunities for European citizens and businesses. A larger Union is an opportunity to enhance energy security and to promote higher environmental, social and consumer standards. Most importantly, as the co-rapporteurs are stating, a larger Union, if well managed, will be the opportunity to expand and anchor democracy, the rule of law and respect of human rights across our continent. However, for these benefits to materialise, full and sustained political commitment is required from all sides. First and foremost, enlargement is and will remain a merit-based process. It requires major efforts by the candidate countries, and for the EU itself, we must show the same determination.

Name: Danuta Maria Hübner
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: European enlargement policy is a powerful tool to promote democracy, the rule of law, respect of fundamental rights. It also gives the EU a stronger voice on the world stage. For aspiring countries, a credible, merit-based prospect of EU membership is the key driver of transformation. Striving to join the European Community, they see the EU membership as a geostrategic investment in prosperity, stability and security based on common European values. Becoming part of the largest single market in the world opens doors for businesses to expand, innovate, invest and create new jobs. Recent rebooting of the enlargement policy after the aggression of Russia has a geopolitical logic. It will expand the democratic space on our continent and make it clear to Russia what is our preferred political order in Europe...European enlargement has always been a ‘win-win’ situation for the Union and the newcomers.

Name: Danuta Maria Hübner
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Recent rebooting of the enlargement policy after the aggression of Russia has a geopolitical logic. It will expand the democratic space on our continent and make it clear to Russia what is our preferred political order in Europe...The EU has committed to stand with Ukraine every step of the way towards the end of the war and the accession. We expect from the Commission to step up the efforts and proceed swiftly and timely with all the phases of accession process, and provide the negotiating framework by mid-March. Indeed, history is watching us.

Name: Thomas Waitz
Party: The Greens – Europeans Free Alliance (Greens – EFA)
Quote: Yes, there’s also geostrategic reasons for us to speed up the candidacy process, but we, in this report, state very clearly that Copenhagen criteria have to be the basis of negotiation and of an accession process.

Name: Jean-Lin Lacapelle
Party: Identity and Democracy (ID)
Quote: we are discussing for the last time before the European elections the enlargement of the European Union, which you wish to extend to countries from the Balkans to Georgia, including Moldova, Ukraine, and even Turkey. Allow me, therefore, also for the last time, to remind you why we strongly oppose this...Secondly, we oppose these enlargements because they compromise the security of our nations and our compatriots. How can we be reassured by integrating into Europe Albania and its mafia, Kosovo and its Islamist majority, Ukraine in full war, which we know would also mean the death of our French farmers, or Turkey, which with its 85 million inhabitants would become the most populous country in Europe and threaten the balance of our civilization? Finally, this ideological obsession you have to integrate what in no way corresponds to our roots and values would accentuate the migratory submersion which we know is for you not a problem but a project. Stop all of this!

Name: Antoni Comín i Oliveres
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)
Quote: Obviously, once candidate countries meet the established criteria, they must be able to join the European Union, because the Union is not a closed club and must keep its doors open to the countries of the Balkans, Ukraine, and so forth. However, this necessary and historic expansion – inevitable – must occur responsibly, and institutional reform of the Council's decision-making system is a precondition for any enlargement.

Name: Antoni Comín i Oliveres
Party: Non-Inscrits (NI)

Name: Andrius Kubilius
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: we answered the Russian aggression against Ukraine with a strong geopolitical move, with an ambitious enlargement agenda, but the whole enlargement process can be very slow. The Western Balkans are an example, and we do not want to repeat it. The process will depend on both sides, on the political will of candidate countries to make reforms, and on the political will of the 27 EU Member States to support enlargement.

Name: Andrius Kubilius
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)

Name: Gabriele Bischoff
Party: Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D)
Quote: if we are truly moving towards the gradual integration of candidate countries, we must do so with the population in mind. I think it is crucial: those who want access to the Single Market must also apply our social standards and our social acquis, otherwise it will lead to widespread social and wage dumping, and the consequences will be borne by EU citizens, as well as workers who come here and work at low wages without proper security.

Name: Dacian Cioloș
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: the European Union has become stronger after each enlargement. All states that integrated into the European Union experienced accelerated economic development post-accession, and we want the same for the Western Balkans, Ukraine, and the Republic of Moldova, which are waiting for similar prospects from us. But for this, the future enlargement must find us prepared, with more efficient European institutions and increased decision-making capacity. We will need to work together, especially with Ukraine, so that the Union can accommodate a large country in the internal market, including the agricultural and agri-food sectors.

Name: Dacian Cioloș

Quote: You have also failed to compel the authorities in Skopje to fulfill your own condition to include Bulgarians in the constitution. This has not happened, and this is a clear and visible failure. You have failed to include in the progress report of North Macedonia the glaring, drastic examples of violence, fires, and attacks against people who identify with Bulgarian national consciousness. What kind of enlargement is this, and what enlargement will there be when in a country that is not even a candidate for membership, authorities crush some people, and these people come to complain and you pretend not to notice them?...You cannot give Ukraine as an example and justify breaking your own rules with Ukraine. It has been said that every country wishing to be a candidate for membership must meet certain criteria. You cannot close your eyes. If you do, you will continue to fail, and we will continue to remind you of it.

Name: Angel Dzhambazki
Party: European Conservatives and Reformists Group (ECR)

It has been said that every country wishing to be a candidate for membership must meet certain criteria. You cannot close your eyes. If you do, you will continue to fail, and we will continue to remind you of it.

Name: Kateřina Konečná
Party: European United Left – Nordic Green Left (GUE – NGL)
Quote: However, enlargement is definitely not needed, and neither are reforms like abolishing unanimity. Does anyone here really feel that the Union, at its current size, is functioning as it should? We suffocate our own industry with green madness, and new industry goes to the United States, to which the EU cannot respond. The Union is unable to hold migrants at its borders and return them home. By supplying arms, we maintain the conflict in Ukraine, which economically destroys us. Corruption reaches the highest levels, and even Mrs. von der Leyen secretly corresponds with Pfizer about vaccine procurement, which member states then pay for. No, the EU is definitely not ready for enlargement, and federalization plans to abolish the veto right must be rejected.

Name: Sunčana Glavak
Party: Group of the European People's Party (EPP)
Quote: Croatia has undeniably been a strong advocate for enlargement, especially of the Western Balkan countries. When we talk about reforms within the European Union, I believe it is extremely important to utilize the current mechanisms available to us to take necessary steps towards Union enlargement. I also want to emphasize the cohesion funds which will be crucial in this process. On the other hand, from candidate countries, we expect to see reforms including judicial independence, economic stability, environmental protection, human rights, and alignment with the EU's external and security policies, which we see lacking in some countries. Every area is crucial for the integration process. Our ultimate goal is not just formal alignment with EU norms, but real internal transformation that will benefit new members after their accession. We must view EU enlargement as a significant link for peace and stability and as an economic strengthening of our Union.

Name: Billy Kelleher
Party: Renew Europe (RE)
Quote: There is no doubt that there are concerns that some countries would not be able to live with the pace of the European economy, but I would like to remind people that Ireland, in 1973 when it joined, was the poorest country in Europe, and at that stage even some European countries opposed our application to join the EU. So I do believe that it is in the interests of the candidate countries as well, but we must ensure that we invest in them now, in terms of institutions, democracy, a functioning market economy and ensuring that they can live with the EU obligations. If we don’t invest in them now, well then we will have significant challenges in convincing citizens within the European Union now that others are welcome into our Union. So I certainly support the concept of enlargement, investment in the candidate countries now, to ensure that they will have the capacity to live within the European Union, and as importantly, European citizens will then be able to embrace them and welcome them.
